definition_zh: 技术员；技师

senses.title: A skilled equipment worker
senses.definition: a person trained to look after equipment or do practical technical work
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、负责设备维护或实际操作技术工作的人
senses.example: The technician opened the machine and checked the wires.
senses.exampleCN: 技师拆开机器，逐根检查线路。
senses.why: The word names the person who owns a craft in practice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指在实践中掌握一门手艺的人。

senses.title: Someone with great skill
senses.definition: a person who performs a skill with unusual control
senses.definitionCN: 技艺控制得格外出色的人
senses.example: As a pianist she is a real technician.
senses.exampleCN: 作为钢琴家，她是真正的技巧大师。
senses.why: Technical skill can be praised in art as well as in repair work.

definition_zh: 技术的；技术上的；由技术引起的；技术先进的
definition_en: relating to technology, or brought about by machines, methods and applied knowledge
core_image: 车间里机械臂沿轨道移动，传感器把每一次位移变成屏幕上的数据点
scene: 车间里机械臂按程序移动，工程师把新装的传感器称为这一轮升级的关键。Technological change reached the workshop long before the office noticed.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「由技术发展带来的变化」（第 3 个义项：由机器、方法与应用知识引起的变化）；句意为技术变化早在办公室察觉之前就到了车间。图中可辨识物件：机械臂、轨道、传感器、数据屏。

pos.zh: 由技术引起的；技术先进的

senses.title: Relating to technology in general
senses.definition: connected with the tools, methods and applied knowledge a society uses
senses.definitionCN: 与社会所使用的工具、方法及应用知识有关
senses.example: Technological change reached the workshop long before the office noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 技术变化早在办公室察觉之前就到了车间。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun for the study of crafts to any subject it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把表示「技艺之学」的名词挂到它所描述的对象上。

senses.title: Advanced in equipment or method
senses.titleCN: 技术先进的；装备水平高的
senses.definition: equipped with or relying on a high level of machinery and method
senses.definitionCN: 装备或依赖高水平机器与方法的
senses.example: Their newest line is highly technological, with sensors at every station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最新的生产线技术含量很高，每个工位都有传感器。
senses.why: A plant that depends on many devices can be described by the adjective, so 'related to technology' shades into 'full of it'.
senses.whyCN: 依赖大量装置的工厂可以用这个形容词描述，于是「与技术有关」滑向「技术密集」。

senses.title: Caused by technology
senses.definition: brought about by machines or new methods rather than by nature or policy
senses.definitionCN: 由机器或新方法而非自然或政策造成的
senses.example: Technological unemployment follows when machines replace routine tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 当机器取代常规工作时，就会出现技术性失业。
senses.why: Once the adjective marks a cause, it can label effects that would not exist without the tools.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词标记原因时，它就能给那些离开工具便不会存在的后果贴标签。

senses.title: Pertaining to the limits of equipment
senses.definition: concerning what the available tools and methods can or cannot do
senses.definitionCN: 涉及现有工具与方法能做到或做不到什么
senses.example: The boundary is technological rather than legal.
senses.exampleCN: 这道界限是技术上的，而非法律上的。
senses.why: A limit set by tools is distinct from one set by law, and the adjective separates the two causes.
senses.whyCN: 工具造成的限制与法律造成的限制不同，这个形容词把两种原因分开。

senses.title: Demanding technical skill
senses.definition: requiring specialised method or skill rather than ordinary handling
senses.definitionCN: 需要专门方法或技艺，而非一般操作的
senses.example: Dyeing is the most technological step in the whole process.
senses.exampleCN: 染色是整个流程中技术性最强的一步。
senses.why: Where a step depends on exact methods, it is technological in the older sense of belonging to a craft.
senses.whyCN: 当一道步骤依赖精确方法时，它在「属于一门技艺」的较早意义上就是技术性的。

senses.title: Belonging to technical research
senses.definition: of the branch of work that develops tools and processes, as distinct from pure science
senses.definitionCN: 指开发工具与工艺的那类工作，与纯科学相区别
senses.example: Technological research and pure science answer different questions.
senses.exampleCN: 技术研究与纯科学回答的是不同的问题。
senses.why: Research aimed at making things work is separated from research aimed at understanding, and the adjective marks the first.
senses.whyCN: 以让东西能用为目标的研究，与以理解为目标的研究被区分开，这个形容词标记前者。

senses.title: Treating tools as the driver of history
senses.definition: in social theory, explaining change chiefly by the state of the tools
senses.definitionCN: 在社会理论中，主要以工具状况解释变化
senses.example: A technological view of history makes tools the driver of change.
senses.exampleCN: 一种技术论的历史观把工具当作变化的驱动力。
senses.why: When the adjective modifies a view rather than a thing, it claims that technology causes history.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词修饰的是一种观点而非物件时，它主张技术造成了历史。

senses.title: Pertaining to craft skill in restoration
senses.definition: concerning the manual and material knowledge needed to preserve or repair objects
senses.definitionCN: 涉及保存或修复物件所需的手工与材料知识
senses.example: The restoration needed technological skill as much as taste.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修复既需要品味，也同样需要工艺技术。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is craft, so repair work that depends on material knowledge is technological too.
senses.whyCN: 词根最古老的意思是技艺，因此依赖材料知识的修复工作同样属于技术层面。

intro.en: Technological joins a Greek noun for craft to a Greek suffix for study, and only in the modern period did it come to mean machines. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个希腊语中表示「技艺」的名词连到表示「学问」的后缀上，直到近代才用来指机器。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tekhne meant 'craft, skill, art', the knowledge of how to make something. Its earlier origin is reconstructed from a root often glossed 'to weave or fabricate', so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: tekhne 意为「技艺、技能、手艺」，即知道如何制作某物。其更早来源由常被解释为「编织、制作」的词根重构而来，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix -logia meant 'the study or account of', from logos 'word, reason, reckoning'.
items.cn: 后缀 -logia 意为「对……的论述或研究」，出自 logos「言词、理性、计算」。

items.en: Tekhnologia in Greek meant a systematic treatment of an art, not the art of machines.
items.cn: 希腊语 tekhno-logia 指对某门技艺的系统论述，而不是机器之术。

items.en: English technology first named a discourse on an art; the sense of practical arts and then machines developed later.
items.cn: 这个词最初指对一门技艺的论述；实用技艺义、再到机器义是后来发展的。

items.en: The adjective appeared in the nineteenth century, when industry began to be described in terms of applied knowledge and machinery.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现于十九世纪，当时人们开始用应用知识与机械来描述工业。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek root with different jobs, which are constantly confused; group two holds adjectives for advanced or machine-based work.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词根但分工不同的词，最易混淆；第二组是表示先进或机器化的形容词。

entries.definition: Belonging to a particular craft or to the mechanical details of a subject; a technical fault is a small mechanical one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一门技艺或某一主题的机械细节；技术故障指小的机械问题。

entries.definition: A way of doing something skilfully; it is the craft itself, not the adjective of relation.
entries.definitionCN: 熟练做某事的方法，是手艺本身，而非表示关系的形容词。

entries.definition: The body of tools, methods and knowledge; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 工具、方法与知识的整体，形容词描述属于它的东西。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used of processes and states rather than of things.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，多用于过程与状态，而非物件。

entries.definition: Far along in development; it praises the level without naming the tools.
entries.definitionCN: 发展程度高，赞的是水平，不点明所用工具。

entries.definition: Working through numerical signals; it is narrower than technological and names a family of devices.
entries.definitionCN: 通过数字信号工作，比「技术的」窄，指一族装置。

entries.definition: Belonging to manufacturing on a large scale; a technological change need not be industrial.
entries.definitionCN: 属于大规模制造，技术变化未必是工业的。

entries.definition: Driven by physical parts; it covers only one part of what the adjective covers.
entries.definitionCN: 由物理部件驱动，只覆盖这个形容词所指的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Greek noun for craft plus a suffix for systematic study: the adjective describes whatever belongs to that study.
normal.cn: 希腊语「技艺」名词加表示系统学问的后缀：这个形容词描述属于这门学问的一切。

normal.en: The family runs technology, technologist, technically, technique and the adverb in -ly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括技术、技术专家、技术性地、技巧，以及加副后缀的形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the theme: change, development, innovation, advance, progress, breakthrough.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出主题：技术变革、技术发展、技术创新、技术进步、技术进展、技术突破。

normal.en: The root meant craft long before it meant machines, which is why a restorer's skill is also called technological.
normal.cn: 词根在指机器之前很久就指技艺，因此修复师的手艺也算技术层面。

normal.en: Keep the pair apart: technical points to a detail or a craft, technological points to the system of tools.
normal.cn: 要分清这一对：一个指向细节或某门手艺，另一个指向工具系统。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that once held a chisel and now holds a controller.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手，从前握着凿子，如今握着控制器。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every movement leaves a trace on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一间车间，每个动作都在屏幕上留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture a timetable that changes because a machine changed, not because anyone voted.
abstract.cn: 想象一份时刻表因一台机器改变而改变，而不是因为有人投票。

examples.en: The gap between rich and poor regions is partly technological.
examples.cn: 富区与穷区之间的差距有一部分是技术上的。

examples.en: Technological advances in cooling made the desert farm possible.
examples.cn: 制冷技术的进步使沙漠农场成为可能。

examples.en: The report treats technological and legal barriers separately.
examples.cn: 报告把技术障碍与法律障碍分开处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「techno（技艺）+ logical（学问的）」——关于技艺之学的 → 技术的、技术引起的

root: 希腊语「技艺」名词加表示「系统学问」的后缀，再加形容词后缀；该名词的更早来源属重构形式，通常解释为「编织、制作」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: it points at tools in general, then at a high level of them, then at effects they cause, at limits they set, at skill they demand, at the research that improves them, at a theory that makes them the cause of history, and finally at the old craft sense of skilled hands.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：先泛指工具，再指工具水平高，接着指工具造成的后果、设定的限制、要求的技艺、改进它们的研究、把它们当作历史动因的理论，最后回到「巧手之艺」的古老含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mechanical arm moving along a rail while a sensor turns each movement into a point of light on a screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：机械臂沿轨道移动，传感器把每一次位移变成屏幕上的一个光点。

branches.en: TOOLS IN GENERAL AND TOOLS IN PLENTY: the broad relation and the high level differ only in degree.
branches.cn: 泛指工具与工具密集：宽泛的关系与高水平只差程度。

branches.en: TOOLS AS CAUSE: an effect on employment and a theory of history both make the tool the reason.
branches.cn: 工具作为原因：对就业的影响与对历史的解释，都把工具当作理由。

branches.en: TOOLS AS LIMIT AND AS DEMAND: what equipment cannot do and what skill it requires are two faces of one constraint.
branches.cn: 工具作为限制与要求：设备做不到的事与它要求的技艺，是同一约束的两面。

branches.en: IMPROVING THE TOOLS: research aimed at better tools is the engine of the whole chain.
branches.cn: 改进工具：以更好的工具为目标的研究，是整条链条的发动机。

branches.en: THE OLD CRAFT: restoration returns the word to skilled hands and materials.
branches.cn: 古老的技艺：修复工作把这个词带回巧手与材料。

intro.en: Technological is built from a Greek noun of craft, a Greek suffix of study and a Latin-shaped adjective ending, so three layers meet in one word.

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin technologia carried the Greek compound into learned writing, and Late Latin technicus supplied the adjective of craft.

items.example: The ending makes the adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The adjective appeared when industry was described as applied knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词出现于人们用应用知识描述工业之时。

entries.definition: two small telescopes for both eyes
entries.definitionCN: 双筒望远镜

entries.definition: a curved piece that bends light
entries.definitionCN: 镜片

normalIntro.en: Telescope means far-looking, and its sections slide like its name.
normalIntro.cn: telescope 意为「看远处」，它的各节也像名字一样套缩。

normal.en: He pointed the telescope at the moon.
normal.cn: 他把望远镜对准月亮。

normal.en: She telescoped the umbrella at the door.
normal.cn: 她在门口收拢雨伞。

normal.en: The radio telescope listens to the sky.
normal.cn: 射电望远镜聆听天空。

normal.en: The two meetings telescoped into one hour.
normal.cn: 两场会议压缩成一小时。

normal.en: A space telescope orbits the earth.
normal.cn: 一台空间望远镜绕地球运行。

abstract.en: Far things come near through a tube.
abstract.cn: 远处的事物通过一根筒靠近。

abstract.en: Folding is looking, in a smaller shape.
abstract.cn: 套叠就是以更小的形状「看」。

abstract.en: Space can be pushed into less space.
abstract.cn: 空间可以被压进更小的空间。

examples.en: He pointed the telescope at the moon in the night sky.
examples.cn: 他把望远镜对准夜空中的那轮月亮。

examples.en: She telescoped the umbrella and stepped inside.
examples.cn: 她收拢雨伞，走进屋里。

examples.en: The two meetings telescoped into one short hour.
examples.cn: 两场会议被压缩成一个短小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太远看不见，使个筒」——远处看不清，就使个筒子看，正是望远镜。

root: 希腊语 tele（远）加 skopein（观看）构成，经意大利语 telescopio 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Telescope names the far-seeing tube, then the sliding of its sections, then any compression.
sensesIntro.cn: telescope 先指看远的筒，再指各节套缩，再指任何压缩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long tube pointed at the moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长筒对准月亮。

branches.en: The instrument is the main sense.
branches.cn: 仪器是主要义项。

branches.en: Sliding sections come from the tube.
branches.cn: 套缩动作来自筒身。

branches.en: Compression borrows the same image.
branches.cn: 压缩借用同一形象。

branches.en: Instrument and folding are one design.
branches.cn: 仪器与套叠源于同一设计。

branches.en: Both save space.
branches.cn: 两者都节省空间。

intro.en: Telescope pairs with microscope and other -scope words.
intro.cn: telescope 与 microscope 等 -scope 词并列。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin; Latin supplies visio for related sight words.
latinIntro.cn: 该词源自希腊语；拉丁语 visio 提供相关「看」的词根。

definition_zh: 脾气；情绪；坏心情；回火；韧性；使缓和；调和
definition_en: a person's state of mind, especially regarding anger; also the hardness of metal, or to soften something
core_image: 一块烧红的铁被浸入冷水，狠劲收成了刚韧
scene: 铁匠把烧红的刀刃浸进水里，狠狠的火气一下子被驯服。The blacksmith used cold water to temper the hot blade.
sceneCN: 这里 temper 是动词「回火、使刚柔并济」（第 5 个义项：锻炼金属性格）；句意：铁匠用冷水给灼热的刀刃回火。

derivatives.zh: 气质；性情（由 temper 加名词后缀构成，指人与生俱来的心性配比）
温和的；有节制的；温带的（形容词，指情绪或气候有分寸）
温度（同根名词，指冷热程度的「适度」读数）
无节制的；放纵的（加否定前缀 in- 构成）

senses.title: A state of mind or mood
senses.definition: the particular state of mind someone is in at a moment
senses.definitionCN: 某人一时的情绪状态
senses.example: She is in a cheerful temper today.
senses.exampleCN: 她今天心情很好。
senses.why: The core is a proper mixture: a mood is the current blend inside a person, measured like a mix of ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 核心是「恰当的调配」：心情就是人此刻体内的配比状态，像混合物般可浓可淡。

senses.title: The tendency to become angry
senses.definition: a tendency to become angry easily, especially in lose or keep one's temper
senses.definitionCN: 易怒的倾向，多用于 lose/keep one's temper
senses.example: He lost his temper when the file was deleted.
senses.exampleCN: 文件被删后他发了火。
senses.why: Anger is the mixture boiling over: losing temper means the blend escapes its measure.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒是配比沸腾溢出：lose one's temper 就是情绪冲出了它的「分寸」。

senses.title: The hardness of a metal
senses.definition: the degree of hardness and elasticity given to steel by heating and cooling
senses.definitionCN: 钢经加热冷却后获得的硬度与弹性
senses.example: The blade has a fine temper.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀刃韧性极佳。
senses.why: Metal treated by fire and water holds the same idea: qualities mixed to the right degree.
senses.whyCN: 金属经水火处理仍循同一理念：把种种性质调配到恰当程度。

senses.title: Make something less severe
senses.definition: to make a feeling or action less strong by mixing in something gentler
senses.definitionCN: 掺入较温和的成分使情感或做法变得不那么激烈
senses.example: His anger was tempered by humour.
senses.exampleCN: 幽默冲淡了他的怒气。
senses.why: To temper literally means to mix in due proportion; softening is adding a mild ingredient to the blend.
senses.whyCN: temper 的字面义是「按比例调和」；缓和就是往混合物里加一味温性的成分。

senses.title: Harden metal by heating and cooling
senses.definition: to heat and cool metal to give it the required hardness
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热与冷却使金属达到所需的硬度
senses.example: The smith tempered the blade in cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 铁匠在冷水中给刀刃回火。
senses.why: The workshop sense is the mixture made physical: fire, water and metal blended into toughness.
senses.whyCN: 工坊义把「调配」落到实物：火、水与金属被调和成刚韧之材。

senses.title: A bad mood, an angry state
senses.definition: an occasion of sudden anger, as in a fit of temper
senses.definitionCN: 一阵突然的怒气，用于 a fit of temper
senses.example: The child threw a fit of temper in the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子在店里大发脾气。
senses.why: When the mixture boils fully, the outburst itself is called a temper: a storm of the blend.
senses.whyCN: 当配比彻底沸腾，爆发的怒气本身也被称作 temper：一场情绪风暴。

intro.en: Temper comes from Latin temperare, to mix in due proportion, the same verb that gives temperature and temperate.
intro.cn: temper 源自拉丁语 temperare「按适当比例调和」，与 temperature、temperate 同源。

items.en: Temperare meant to mix properly, to keep a thing within due measure.
items.cn: temperare 意为妥善调配，使事物保持在适当限度内。

items.en: The deeper origin of temperare is debated; a link with tempus, time or season, is often proposed but not proven.
items.cn: temperare 的更早来源有争议；常被联系到 tempus「时间、时节」，但并未确证。

items.en: The word entered Old English as temprian through church Latin, first of timbers and then of minds.
items.cn: 该词经教会拉丁语进入古英语作 temprian，先指木料调配，后指心性。

items.en: Mood, anger and the blending of qualities all gathered under temper.
items.cn: 中世纪英语中，情绪、怒气与性质调配都汇入 temper。

items.en: Metalworkers gave temper its workshop sense, and psychology kept the mood sense.
items.cn: 近代金工赋予 temper 回火义，而心理层面保留情绪义。

note.en: Temper sits in a large family of mixing words; the first group shows the family, the second the near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: temper 属庞大的「调和」词族；第一组展示词族，第二组展示近义。

entries.definition: the degree of heat, from the same mixing verb
entries.definitionCN: 温度；出自同一「调和」动词

entries.definition: mild and self-restrained
entries.definitionCN: 温和有节的；温带的

entries.definition: a person's inborn disposition
entries.definitionCN: 气质；与生俱来的性情

entries.definition: the way someone feels at a time
entries.definitionCN: 某人一时的心情状态

entries.definition: to make something less extreme
entries.definitionCN: 使缓和；使不过激

entries.definition: to make something less hard or severe
entries.definitionCN: 使变软；使缓和

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin temperare, the temperate-temperature family, the smith's quench, and keep or lose one's temper.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁 temperare、temperate/temperature 词族、铁匠淬火、keep/lose one's temper。

normal.en: Temperare means to mix in the right measure; a temper is your current mix.
normal.cn: temperare 意为按比例调和；temper 就是你当下的「配比」。

normal.en: Keep your temper: keep the blend inside its measure.
normal.cn: keep your temper：让情绪配比留在分寸之内。

normal.en: Tempered steel is fire and water mixed into toughness.
normal.cn: 回火钢是火与水调和出的韧性。

normal.en: Temper justice with mercy: blend the two in due proportion.
normal.cn: 宽严并济：把两者按比例调和。

normal.en: Temperature measures how far the mix of heat leans either way.
normal.cn: temperature 测量冷热配比偏向哪一侧。

abstract.en: Every temper is a recipe written in mood.
abstract.cn: 每种脾气都是用情绪写成的配方。

abstract.en: The smith and the angry man work on the same metal: heat, then give it shape.
abstract.cn: 铁匠与发怒的人面对同一块金属：先加热，再塑形。

abstract.en: Moderation is a mixing bowl all people carry.
abstract.cn: 节制是人人都随身携带的一只调羹盆。

examples.en: Try to keep your temper during the argument.
examples.cn: 争论中尽量忍住脾气。

examples.en: The steel was tempered to just the right hardness.
examples.cn: 这块钢被回火到恰到好处的硬度。

examples.en: Her criticism was tempered with kindness.
examples.cn: 她的批评里掺着善意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太泼」——太泼辣的性子要回火降温，泼劲被调和 → temper 脾气、使缓和

root: 拉丁语 temperare「按适当比例调和、使适度」；名词指调配的结果（心情配比、金属回火度），动词指进行调配（使缓和、回火）。

sensesIntro.en: From mixing to the right measure come the mood blend, the boiling temper, the tempered blade, and gentled words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「调配适度」长出心情的配比、沸腾的火气、回火的刀刃与放缓的言辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blend kept to its proper measure.
core.cn: 核心意象：被控制在恰当比例里的一味混合物。

branches.en: The blend is the mood; boiling over is the fit.
branches.cn: 配比即心情；沸腾即发作。

branches.en: A quick temper is a blend near boiling point.
branches.cn: 急脾气是接近沸点的配比。

branches.en: Adding a mild ingredient cools the mixture.
branches.cn: 加一味温和成分使混合物降温。

branches.en: Fire, water and steel are blended into resilience.
branches.cn: 火、水与钢被调和成韧性。

branches.en: Justice and mercy meet in one bowl.
branches.cn: 宽与严在同一只碗里相遇。

intro.en: Temper heads a Latin family of measuring and mixing words, from temperature to temperament.
intro.cn: temper 是拉丁语「度量与调和」词族的头目，从 temperature 到 temperament。

latinIntro.en: Latin temperare, to mix in due proportion, may be linked with tempus, time or season; the connection is proposed but not certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 temperare「按比例调和」常被联系到 tempus「时间、时节」，此说未获确证。

items.meaning: the act of hardening or softening

items.meaningCN: 木材；仅拼写与 temper 相近

definition_zh: 气质；性情；易激动的脾性；气质类型说；平均律（音乐）
definition_en: the usual temper of a person or animal, or the tuning of an instrument to a settled system
core_image: 四种不同温度的水倒进同一只杯子，杯子不变，杯里的冷热却决定了它适合装什么
scene: 同一个班里，一个孩子跌倒后自己爬起来继续跑，另一个要人抱很久才肯下地，老师记住了这两个名字。Thirty years later the teacher still described them by temperament rather than by grades.
sceneCN: 这里 temperament 指「一个人天生而稳定的性情倾向」（第 1 个义项：稳定的人格气质）；句意是三十年后老师仍按性情、而不是按成绩来描述这两个人。图中可辨识物件：操场、自己爬起的孩子、被抱着的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 气质的；喜怒无常的；性能不稳定的

senses.title: A settled natural disposition
senses.definition: the usual balance of a person's nature, especially as it shows in how they react
senses.definitionCN: 一个人天性的通常配比，尤其体现在反应方式上
senses.example: The teacher described them by temperament rather than by grades.
senses.exampleCN: 老师按性情而不是按成绩来描述他们。
senses.why: the word began as a word for a due mixture, so it names a ratio inside a person that stays roughly the same across situations.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「恰当的混合」，因此命名的是人体内一个在各种情境下大致不变的配比。

senses.title: A tendency to flare up
senses.definition: the part of a disposition that decides how quickly anger or excitement rises
senses.definitionCN: 决定愤怒或兴奋升起多快的那部分性情
senses.example: He has the temperament of a kettle that whistles early.
senses.exampleCN: 他的脾性像一只早早叫起来的水壶。
senses.why: heat is one of the oldest images in this word, which is why it so often appears with fiery or calm.
senses.whyCN: 「热」是这个词最古老的意象之一，因此它常与「火爆」或「沉静」连用。

senses.title: One of the four old types
senses.titleCN: 旧说中的四种类型之一
senses.definition: a category in the ancient theory that divided people by the balance of bodily humours
senses.definitionCN: 古代按体液配比给人分类的那套理论中的一个类别
senses.example: The four temperaments were once taught as medical fact.
senses.exampleCN: 四种气质类型曾被当作医学事实讲授。
senses.why: classical medicine explained character by the mixture of fluids in the body, and the word still carries that taxonomy.
senses.whyCN: 古典医学用体内液体的混合来解释性格，这个词至今带着那套分类。

senses.title: A system of tuning
senses.definition: a way of tuning instruments so that the notes stay in usable relations across keys
senses.definitionCN: 一种调音方式，使各音在各调之间保持可用的关系
senses.example: Equal temperament made the piano a flexible instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 十二平均律让钢琴成为一件灵活的乐器。
senses.why: in music the word keeps its literal sense of adjusting a mixture until it balances, applied here to intervals.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，这个词保留了「把混合调到平衡」的字面义，只是把对象换成了音程。

senses.title: An animal's handling
senses.titleCN: 动物的性子与好不好带
senses.definition: the disposition of an animal, especially as it affects how easily it can be worked with
senses.definitionCN: 动物的性情，尤其影响它好不好驾驭
senses.example: The breed is chosen for a steady temperament around children.
senses.exampleCN: 选这个品种，是因为它在孩子身边性子稳。
senses.why: the word applies wherever a creature has a fixed setting, which is why breeders use it like a specification.
senses.whyCN: 凡是有固定「设定」的生物都适用这个词，因此育种者拿它当规格来用。

senses.title: The temper of an age
senses.definition: the prevailing character of a period or a group, spoken of as if it were a person
senses.definitionCN: 某个时期或群体的主导性格，被当作一个人来说
senses.example: Historians speak of the temperament of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 史学家会谈那十年的时代脾气。
senses.why: the metaphor of a body with balanced fluids transfers easily to a collective, which is how whole eras get a temper.
senses.whyCN: 「体内液体平衡」这一比喻很容易搬到集体上，整个时代于是有了脾气。

senses.title: The fit between parts
senses.definition: the working balance among mixed elements, as in a blend or an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 混合成分之间起作用的配比，如调配或布局
senses.example: The garden's temperament comes from the ratio of stone to green.
senses.exampleCN: 这座园子的脾性来自石头与绿意的配比。
senses.why: this sense reaches back to the original meaning of a measured mixture and keeps the word's earliest image alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项回到「按量混合」的本义，让这个词最早的意象继续活着。

senses.title: A temperamental machine
senses.definition: the use of the derived adjective for equipment that works only when it feels like it
senses.definitionCN: 用其派生形容词指只在它高兴时才肯工作的设备
senses.example: The old press is temperamental in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 那台老印刷机天冷时脾气很坏。
senses.why: machines are described with this family because they are treated as having a disposition, which is the joke the usage rests on.
senses.whyCN: 机器被用这一词族来描述，是因为它们被当作有性情，这个用法正建立在这个玩笑上。

intro.en: Temperament comes from Latin temperamentum 'a due mixture', from temperare 'to mix in proportion, to moderate'. Classical medicine used it for the balance of bodily humours, and music borrowed it for the tuning of intervals. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: temperament 来自拉丁 temperamentum「恰当的混合」，出自 temperare「按比例调配、节制」。古典医学用它指体液配比，音乐则借它指音程的调校。年代均为约数。

items.en: Temperare meant 'to divide or mix in due proportion, to moderate'. A suggested link to tempus 'time' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: temperare 意为「按适当比例调和、节制」。有人认为它与意为「时间」的词有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The noun named the resulting balance, first of climate and of bodily fluids, later of any mixture.
items.cn: 这个名词指混合后的平衡，先是气候与体液，后来是任何混合。

items.en: Greek and then Latin medicine explained health and character by four fluids, so temperament became a medical word for a person's constitutional balance.
items.cn: 希腊继而拉丁医学用四种液体解释健康与性格，于是 temperament 成为指个人体质配比的医学词。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century for a person's habitual disposition, and the older medical theory faded while the word stayed.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个词，指一个人惯常的性情；旧医学理论衰落，词却留了下来。

items.en: From the seventeenth century musicians used it for the tuning of intervals, where a tempered system is one deliberately adjusted to balance.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，音乐家用它指音程的调校，所谓「调律体系」就是刻意调整以求平衡的系统。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of temperare is a reconstruction, and the exact date of the musical use is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：temperare 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，音乐义的确切年代也未定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin verb of mixing, which differ sharply in meaning; group two holds the words for character that psychologists keep apart.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「调配」动词、意义却相差很远的词；第二组是心理学家刻意区分的性格词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb through a noun for a tempered state: it measures heat, not character, and the resemblance is purely historical.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个拉丁动词，经一个表调匀状态的名词而来：它量的是热度，不是性格，相似纯属历史同源。

entries.definition: The shorter relative: as a noun it means a tendency to anger, as a verb to soften or moderate something.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的亲属词：作名词指易怒的倾向，作动词指使变软或使缓和。

entries.definition: The adjective of restraint, used of climate, habits and speech; it describes moderation rather than an inborn balance.
entries.definitionCN: 指有节制的形容词，用于气候、习惯与言谈；它描述的是节制，而不是天生的配比。

entries.definition: Built on this noun: it can mean 'of temperament' but is used far more often for people or machines that change behaviour abruptly.
entries.definitionCN: 由本名词构成：可指「性情的」，但更常用于形容人或机器行为突然多变。

entries.definition: The total pattern of traits and behaviour built over a life; temperament is the part thought to be inborn and stable.
entries.definitionCN: 一生中形成的特质与行为的总格局；temperament 是其中被认为天生而稳定的那一部分。

entries.definition: A settled readiness to behave in a certain way; it is less biological in tone than temperament.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种方式行事的固定倾向；在语气上不如 temperament 那样带生理色彩。

entries.definition: The moral shape of a person, judged as strong or weak; temperament says nothing about virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的道德形状，可评为坚强或软弱；temperament 与德行无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for what someone is like by birth; it is broader and carries no theory of humours.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人天生怎样的日常词；更宽，也不带任何体液理论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb behind it means 'to mix in due proportion', so a temperament is a recipe that came out balanced.
normal.cn: 背后的拉丁动词意为「按比例调配」，因此气质就是一份调得刚好的配方。

normal.en: The family runs temperament, temperamental, temperamentally, temper, temperate, temperature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 temperament、temperamental、temperamentally、temper、temperate、temperature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: a calm temperament, by temperament, an artistic temperament.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：沉静的气质、就性情而言、艺术家的脾性。

normal.en: Equal temperament is the musical sense, where intervals are adjusted to balance.
normal.cn: 十二平均律是音乐义，那里音程被调校以求平衡。

normal.en: The four temperaments come from the old medicine of bodily humours.
normal.cn: 四种气质类型来自旧的体液医学。

abstract.en: Picture four cups of water at different temperatures poured into one glass.
abstract.cn: 想象四杯不同温度的水倒进同一只杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle whose whistle comes at different moments for different owners.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水壶，对不同主人有不同的鸣叫时刻。

abstract.en: Picture a piano tuned so that every key agrees to compromise.
abstract.cn: 想象一架钢琴被调成每个键都同意让步。

examples.en: By temperament she is patient, though the work tests her daily.
examples.cn: 就性情而言她很有耐心，尽管这份工作每天在考验她。

examples.en: The two brothers share a temperament but not a vocabulary.
examples.cn: 两兄弟性情相同，说话方式却完全不同。

examples.en: Equal temperament allows a keyboard instrument to play in every key.
examples.cn: 十二平均律让键盘乐器能在所有调上演奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: temper（调和）+ ament（东西）——把身体里的冷热调成一配方 → 气质、性情

root: 拉丁 temperamentum「恰当的混合」，出自 temperare「按比例调配、节制」；古典医学用它指体液配比，音乐借它指调律。与表「时间」的词是否有联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a mixture is brought into balance, and that balance is then read as a person's settled nature, as heat, as one of four types, as a tuning system, as an animal's setting, as the temper of an age, as a ratio among parts and finally as a machine's whims.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：混合物被调到平衡，这个平衡依次被读作一个人稳定的天性、热度、四种类型之一、一套调律、动物的设定、一个时代的脾气、各部分之间的配比，最后是机器的任性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four waters at different temperatures poured into one glass, so the glass decides what it can hold.
core.cn: 核心意象：四杯不同温度的水倒进同一只杯子，杯子于是决定了它能装什么。

branches.en: THE RATIO AND ITS HEAT: the settled mixture first, then the question of how quickly it boils.
branches.cn: 配比与热度：先是定下来的混合，再是它多快沸腾。

branches.en: THE OLD TAXONOMY: the mixture turned into named types by classical medicine.
branches.cn: 旧的分类：古典医学把这种混合变成几个有名字的类型。

branches.en: BALANCE APPLIED TO SOUND: music adjusts intervals by the same logic of compromise.
branches.cn: 平衡用于声音：音乐用同一套让步的逻辑来调音程。

branches.en: SETTINGS EVERYWHERE: an animal's handling and a garden's ratio are the same idea read on other objects.
branches.cn: 各处的设定：动物的性子与园子的配比，是同一观念读在别的对象上。

branches.en: FROM AN AGE TO A MACHINE: collectives and equipment get a temper, and the metaphor stretches until it becomes a joke.
branches.cn: 从时代到机器：集体与设备都得到了脾气，比喻一路拉伸，直到成了玩笑。

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of mixing plus a Latin noun-forming element, and the same pieces recur across a large family.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁「调配」动词加一个拉丁名词构词成分搭成，同样的成分反复出现在一大族词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin temperare gives temper, temperament, temperate and temperature, all through the idea of bringing something to a due measure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 temperare 衍生 temper、temperament、temperate、temperature，全部经由「把某物调到适当的度」这一观念。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea of a measured mixture.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「按量混合」的意思。

items.meaning: means or result of an action
items.example: It turns the verb into the name of a resulting balance.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个动词变成调好之后的平衡的名称。

items.meaning: a due mixture, a balanced state
items.example: The noun first described climate and body fluids.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初描述气候与体液。

items.example: The press is temperamental in winter.
items.exampleCN: 那台印刷机天冷时脾气很坏。
他们在性情上并不合适。

items.meaning: a tendency to anger; to moderate
items.example: He lost his temper at the gate.
The same root measures heat elsewhere.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根在别处用来量热度。

items.example: A temperate climate suits the crop.
items.exampleCN: 温和的气候适合这种作物。

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, moderate
a tempering, due mixture; later, heat level
latinEntries.meaningCN: 调和；适当混合；后指热度

definition_zh: 温度；体温；发烧；气温
definition_en: a measure of how hot or cold something is
core_image: 墙上的温度计里，红色液柱停在一个刻度上，室内外差出一大截
scene: 实验室墙上的温度计显示，室内比室外高许多。The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「可测量的冷热程度」（第 1 个义项：温度读数）；句意为温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。

senses.title: A measured degree of heat
senses.definition: a number expressing how hot or cold a body or space is
senses.definitionCN: 表示物体或空间冷热程度的数值
senses.example: The thermometer showed a temperature ten degrees higher indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示室内温度比室外高十度。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'a tempering or moderation'; early science used it for the balance of hot and cold in a body, then for the measured balance itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「调和、适度」；早期科学用它指体内冷热的平衡，后来指被测出的这个平衡。

senses.title: Body heat
senses.definition: the internal heat of a living body, normally around thirty-seven degrees
senses.definitionCN: 活体内部的温度，正常约三十七度
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's temperature twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天记录病人两次体温。
senses.why: A living body regulates its own balance of heat, which is exactly what the old sense of tempering described.
senses.whyCN: 活体自行调节冷热平衡，这正是旧义「调和」所描述的。

senses.title: The weather figure
senses.definition: the outdoor air temperature reported in a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 预报中报告的室外空气温度
senses.example: The forecast gives a temperature of minus five tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 预报说今晚气温为零下五度。
senses.why: Air is a body too, and meteorology applies the same measurement to the atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 空气也是一种物体，气象学把同一测量用到大气上。

senses.title: A fever
senses.definition: an abnormally high body temperature caused by illness
senses.definitionCN: 疾病引起的异常升高的体温
senses.example: The child has a temperature and should stay home.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子发烧了，应该待在家里。
senses.why: In everyday speech a 'temperature' means the raised figure, not the normal one, so the measurement stands for the illness.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语中 a temperature 指升高的那个数值，而不是正常值，于是测量结果代表了疾病。

senses.title: A device set point
senses.definition: the target temperature set on a thermostat or oven
senses.definitionCN: 在恒温器或烤箱上设定的目标温度
senses.example: Set the temperature to two hundred degrees before baking.
senses.exampleCN: 烘烤前把温度设为两百度。
senses.why: A control dial turns the noun into an instruction: the temperature is what the machine is told to reach.
senses.whyCN: 控制旋钮把这个名词变成指令：温度是机器被要求达到的值。

senses.title: The emotional climate
senses.definition: the general mood or level of tension in a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中的总体情绪或紧张程度
senses.example: The temperature of the debate rose after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 声明发布后，辩论的火气升高了。
senses.why: Social heat is read like physical heat: a room can become hot with anger.
senses.whyCN: 社会的热像物理的热一样被读取：一个房间可以因愤怒而变热。

senses.title: A physical quantity
senses.definition: in physics, a property measuring the average kinetic energy of particles
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中衡量粒子平均动能的属性
senses.example: The temperature of the gas rises as the piston compresses it.
senses.exampleCN: 活塞压缩气体时，气体温度升高。
senses.why: Physics narrows the everyday number to a precise property of a system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把日常数字收窄为系统的精确属性。

senses.title: A standard condition
senses.definition: the ordinary indoor heat at which materials and reactions are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较材料与反应时所用的通常室内温度
senses.example: Store the reagent at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 把试剂存放在室温下。
senses.why: Labs need a standard, so 'room temperature' becomes a fixed benchmark rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 实验室需要一个标准，于是「室温」成了固定基准而不是描述。

intro.en: Temperature comes from Latin temperatura 'a tempering, a due mixture'. The modern physical sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: temperature 出自拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当的混合」。现代物理义是后来的收窄。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Temperatura meant a mixing in due proportion, from temperare 'to mix, regulate, restrain'.
items.cn: temperatura 意为按适当比例混合，出自 temperare「混合、调节、节制」。

items.en: Temperare is related to tempus 'time, season', because mixing in the right measure was imagined as keeping to the right season.
items.cn: temperare 与 tempus「时间、季节」相关，因为「按正确比例混合」被想象为顺应正确的时令。

items.en: Medieval medicine used temperatura for the balanced mixture of humours in a body, and English borrowed it as temperature in this medical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪医学用 temperatura 指体内体液的有序混合，英语借入时也带这一医学义。

items.en: With the thermometer, the word shifted from a balance of qualities to a measurable degree of heat.
items.cn: 随着温度计的发明，这个词从「性质的平衡」转为「可测量的热度」。

items.en: Physics fixed temperature as a quantity, and everyday speech kept the special phrase 'have a temperature' for fever.
items.cn: 物理学把 temperature 固定为一个物理量，日常口语则保留 have a temperature 这一说法指发烧。

items.en: Room temperature and body temperature became standard benchmarks in labs, kitchens and clinics.
items.cn: 室温与体温成为实验室、厨房与诊所的标准基准。

note.en: Group one separates the temperament words from the temperature word; group two holds related measures and sensations.
note.cn: 第一组分辨 temperament 词族与 temperature 的区别；第二组是相关度量与感觉词。

entries.definition: A person's usual character; it comes from the same Latin root, where a balance of humours was thought to shape personality.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人惯常的性格；出自同一拉丁词根，古人认为体液平衡塑造性格。

entries.definition: To moderate or to become angry easily; the noun means a state of mind, not a degree of heat.
entries.definitionCN: 使缓和，或指容易发怒；名词指心境，而不是热度。

entries.definition: Relating to time or to the material world; it comes from tempus 'time', not from temperare.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间或世俗世界有关；出自 tempus「时间」，而非 temperare。

entries.definition: The energy transferred by a difference in temperature; heat is the cause, temperature is the measured result.
entries.definitionCN: 因温差而传递的能量；热是原因，温度是被测出的结果。

entries.definition: A raised body temperature caused by illness; it names the condition, while a temperature is just the reading.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病引起的体温升高；它指病况，而 temperature 只是读数。

entries.definition: The figure shown by an instrument; a temperature is one kind of reading.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器显示的数字；温度是读数的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin family is real, and the measuring instruments are real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁词族真实存在，测量仪器也都是真实复合词。

normal.en: temperature and temperament share temperare: one measures the body's heat, the other names the body's mix of moods.
normal.cn: temperature 与 temperament 共享 temperare：一个测身体的热，一个指身体性情的混合。

normal.en: thermometer = thermo- (heat) + -meter (measure), the instrument that reads a temperature.
normal.cn: thermometer = thermo-「热」+ -meter「测量」，读取温度的仪器。

normal.en: thermostat = thermo- + -stat (standing, holding), a device that holds a set temperature.
normal.cn: thermostat = thermo- + -stat「保持」，把温度保持在设定值的装置。

normal.en: room temperature is the standard phrase in recipes and lab protocols for ordinary indoor heat.
normal.cn: room temperature 是食谱与实验规程中表示通常室内温度的标准说法。

normal.en: to have a temperature means to be feverish, because the number has gone above normal.
normal.cn: have a temperature 指发烧，因为那个数字高出了正常值。

abstract.en: Abstractly, temperature is balance made countable: hot and cold are weighed against each other and turned into a number.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，temperature 是可数的平衡：冷与热相互权衡，变成一个数字。

abstract.en: The same number can describe a room, a body, a gas or the mood of a meeting.
abstract.cn: 同一个数字可以描述房间、身体、气体，也可以描述一场会议的气氛。

abstract.en: So temperature is not heat itself but heat made comparable.
abstract.cn: 所以 temperature 不是热本身，而是变得可比较的热。

examples.en: The temperature fell below zero before dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明前气温降到了零下。

examples.en: Keep the oven at a constant temperature.
examples.cn: 让烤箱保持恒温。

examples.en: Her temperature returned to normal after two days.
examples.cn: 两天后她的体温恢复正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「天不热」：天不热也有温度 → temperature 温度

root: 拉丁语 temperatura「调和、适当混合」← temperare「混合、调节」，与 tempus「时间、季节」相关；十七世纪起经温度计的使用转为可测量的热度。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measurable balance: a room, a body, the weather, a fever, a thermostat setting, a social mood, a physical quantity and a standard benchmark.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一个可测的平衡展开：房间、身体、天气、发烧、恒温设定、群体情绪、物理量，以及标准基准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hot and cold weighed against each other and read off as a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷与热相互权衡，被读成一个数字。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: everyday heat and the physicist's quantity are the same number at two levels of precision.
branches.cn: 测量：日常热度与物理学家的物理量，是同一数字的两种精度。

branches.en: THE BODY: normal warmth and illness-heat are one scale read above and below the usual line.
branches.cn: 身体：正常体温与病热，是同一条刻度在常线上下两侧的读数。

branches.en: THE AIR: a forecast figure and a lab benchmark both describe ordinary surroundings.
branches.cn: 空气：预报数字与实验室基准都在描述平常环境。

branches.en: CONTROL: a dial turns the noun into a target to be reached.
branches.cn: 控制：旋钮把这个名词变成一个要达到的目标。

branches.en: MOOD: a room heated by anger borrows the same thermometer.
branches.cn: 情绪：被愤怒加热的房间借用了同一支温度计。

intro.en: Temperature belongs to the Latin temperare family. English adds -ature for the noun, while Greek thermo- supplies the instruments.
intro.cn: temperature 属于拉丁 temperare 词族。英语加 -ature 构成名词，希腊语 thermo- 则提供仪器名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries below are the recorded ancestors of the family; tempus 'time' is included because temperare was built on the idea of the right season.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁条目是该词族有记录的祖先；列出 tempus「时间」，因为 temperare 建立在「合宜时令」的观念上。

items.meaningCN: 读取温度的仪器（thermo- 表示热，-meter 表示测量）
items.exampleCN: 温度计读数是三十八度。

items.meaning: a device that keeps a set temperature
items.meaningCN: 把温度保持在设定值的装置（-stat 表示保持）
items.example: The thermostat switches the heater off.

items.meaning: to moderate; also a state of mind
items.example: She tempered her criticism with praise.
The temperate zone has four seasons.

items.meaning: kept at a fixed heat by a device
items.example: The samples sit in a temperature-controlled room.

items.meaning: the ordinary indoor heat, used as a benchmark
items.meaningCN: 通常的室内温度，用作基准
items.example: Serve the cheese at room temperature.

items.meaning: the internal heat of a living body
items.example: Body temperature is lowest before dawn.

latinEntries.meaning: to mix in due proportion, regulate

definition_zh: 神庙；寺庙；圣殿；太阳穴；眼镜腿；（文化）殿堂
definition_en: a building used for worship in many religions, or the flat side of the forehead above the cheekbone
core_image: 石柱围出一间内殿，门内是神像，门外是台阶；同一张脸上，眉骨外侧的一处凹陷也叫这个名字
scene: 山道尽头是石阶与断柱，海风穿过柱间。The temple stands on the ridge above the harbour, its columns still unbroken.
sceneCN: 这里 temple 指「供奉神明的神庙」（第 1 个义项：古代宗教建筑）；句意为这座神庙立在海港上方的山脊上，柱身至今未断。图中可辨识物件：石阶、断柱、山脊、海港。

senses.title: A shrine of the old religions
senses.definition: a building dedicated to a god, especially in Greek, Roman or Egyptian worship
senses.definitionCN: 献给某位神明的建筑，尤见于希腊、罗马或埃及崇拜
senses.example: The temple walls still carry the names of donors from three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 神庙墙上仍留着三个世纪以来捐赠者的名字。
senses.why: the oldest sense is a marked-off sacred precinct, and the building is only its most visible part.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是一块被划分出来的神圣地界，建筑只是它最显眼的部分。

senses.title: An East Asian place of worship
senses.definition: a Buddhist, Taoist or Shinto building used for worship and ritual
senses.definitionCN: 佛教、道教或神道用于礼拜与仪式的建筑
senses.example: Incense smoke hangs under the temple eaves all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午，香烟都悬在寺庙的檐下。
senses.why: the word travelled with traders and translators, so it was applied to buildings of religions it never originally named.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随商人与译者旅行，于是被用在它原本从未命名的宗教建筑上。

senses.title: The Temple of Jerusalem
senses.definition: the central sanctuary of ancient Israel, of which only the western retaining wall survives
senses.definitionCN: 古代以色列的中心圣所，今仅存西侧挡土墙
senses.example: Pilgrims still pray at the wall of the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者仍在圣殿的墙边祈祷。
senses.why: in this use the word is almost a proper name: one building, one city, one covenant.
senses.whyCN: 在这一用法中，这个词几乎成了专名：一座建筑、一座城、一份盟约。

senses.title: A Latter-day Saint temple
senses.definition: a building in the Latter-day Saint movement reserved for special ordinances, as distinct from an ordinary meetinghouse
senses.definitionCN: 后期圣徒运动中专供特定仪式的建筑，区别于普通礼拜堂
senses.example: Only members with recommends enter the temple for ordinances.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持推荐书的成员才能进圣殿参加仪式。
senses.why: a new religion kept the old word but narrowed it to one kind of building among several.
senses.whyCN: 一个新宗教沿用了旧词，却把它收窄为若干建筑中的一类。

senses.title: The side of the forehead
senses.definition: the flat area at the side of the forehead above the cheekbone
senses.definitionCN: 额部两侧、颧骨上方的平坦区域
senses.example: The blow landed on his left temple and blurred his vision.
senses.exampleCN: 那一击打在他左侧太阳穴，令视线发花。
senses.why: this is a different Latin word, the plural of the time noun, which in the plural named the temples of the head.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个拉丁词，即「时间」名词的复数形式，其复数专门指头部的太阳穴。

senses.title: The arm of a pair of glasses
senses.definition: the part of a spectacle frame that rests against the side of the head
senses.definitionCN: 眼镜架上贴着头部两侧的部分
senses.example: One temple of the frame was bent after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒之后，镜架的一条腿弯了。
senses.why: eyeglasses are named by the body part they touch, so the anatomical word was transferred to the frame.
senses.whyCN: 眼镜以它所接触的身体部位命名，因此这个解剖词被转用到镜架上。

senses.title: A temple of art or commerce
senses.definition: a large building devoted to a valued activity, described with religious awe
senses.definitionCN: 把某项受珍视的活动说成带有宗教敬畏的大型建筑
senses.example: The old library is a temple of quiet and paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老图书馆是一座安静与纸张的殿堂。
senses.why: the metaphor works because both a temple and a great hall set apart a space from ordinary use.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，因为神庙与宏伟厅堂都把一处空间从日常使用中划分出来。

senses.title: A marked-off piece of sky
senses.titleCN: 古罗马占卜划定的天空区
senses.definition: in Roman augury, a region of the sky marked out for observing signs
senses.definitionCN: 罗马占卜中为观察征兆而划出的一片天空区域
senses.example: The augur divided the temple of the sky into quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 占卜官把这片天空的圣域分成四方。
senses.why: the Latin word began as a space cut off for observation, which is why the building sense and the sky sense share a root.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词最初是为观察而划出的一片空间，因此建筑义与天空义共用同一词根。

intro.en: Two different Latin words lie behind English temple: one means a consecrated space, the other names the temples of the head. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语 temple 背后有两个不同的拉丁词：一个指被祝圣的空间，另一个指头部的太阳穴。年代均为约数。

items.en: Templum meant a space marked out and consecrated for observation, especially by an augur, and only later a shrine building.
items.cn: templum 指划出并祝圣供观察的空间，尤用于占卜，后来才指神庙建筑。

items.en: English borrowed the word early, and it appears in Old English for the Temple of Jerusalem before it named pagan shrines.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个词，古英语中先用于指耶路撒冷圣殿，之后才指异教神庙。

items.en: The plural of the time noun, tempora, was used for the flat places at either side of the forehead, giving the anatomical sense.
items.cn: 表示「时间」的名词其复数 tempora 被用来指额头两侧的平坦处，形成解剖义。

items.en: Translators extended the word to Buddhist and Taoist buildings, so English temple now covers many religions.
items.cn: 译者把这个词扩展到佛教与道教建筑，因此英语 temple 如今涵盖多种宗教。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the anatomical word named the side pieces of eyeglasses, which rest against the temples.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个解剖词被用来命名眼镜架两侧贴着太阳穴的部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the ancestry of templum before Latin is not established; a link to a verb meaning 'to cut' has been proposed, but competing explanations exist and none is proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：templum 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明；有人提出它与表示「切」的动词有关，但存在多种竞争性解释，无一得到证实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like temple or sit in the same semantic field but differ in root; group two holds other sacred buildings.
note.cn: 第一组是与 temple 形近或同属语义场、但词根不同的词；第二组是其他宗教建筑。

entries.definition: A small pattern or gauge used in building; it comes from the same root as template and has nothing to do with worship.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑中用的小样板或规尺，与 template 同源，与礼拜无关。

entries.definition: Relating to time or the material world; it comes from the time noun, which also supplied the plural behind the anatomical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间或世俗世界相关的；来自「时间」名词，该名词的复数又给出了解剖义。

entries.definition: To look at or think about at length; it comes from the Latin verb for observing within a marked-off space.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间注视或思考；来自拉丁语中「在被划出的空间内观察」的动词。

entries.definition: The speed of music, from Italian tempo 'time'; it shares the Latin time noun but not the shrine word.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐的速度，来自意大利语「时间」；与拉丁「时间」名词同源，但与神庙词无关。

entries.definition: A place or receptacle holding something holy, often smaller than a temple and centred on a relic.
entries.definitionCN: 存放圣物之处或容器，常比神庙小，并以圣物为中心。

entries.definition: The holiest room of a religious building or a place of refuge; it stresses protection.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教建筑中最神圣的房间或避难处；强调保护。

entries.definition: A building for Christian worship; temple is used for other traditions and for the Jewish sanctuary.
entries.definitionCN: 基督教礼拜建筑；temple 多用于其他传统或犹太圣所。

entries.definition: A Jewish house of prayer and study; the Temple was the single sanctuary, while synagogues are local.
entries.definitionCN: 犹太人的祈祷与研习之所；圣殿是唯一圣所，会堂则是地方性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Latin sources, the real translation history and the real glasses term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的拉丁语来源、真实的翻译史与真实的眼镜术语。

normal.en: The building sense means a space marked off for a god; the head sense means the flat side of the forehead.
normal.cn: 建筑义指为神划出的空间；头部义指额侧的平坦处。

normal.en: The family runs temple, temples, temple-like, templed, contemplate, contemplation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 temple、temples、temple-like、templed、contemplate、contemplation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: Buddhist temple, temple ruins, the Temple in Jerusalem, temple of art.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：佛寺、神庙遗址、耶路撒冷圣殿、艺术殿堂。

normal.en: The glasses sense is anatomy transferred to an object that touches the same spot.
normal.cn: 眼镜义是把解剖词转用到接触同一部位的物件上。

normal.en: Roman augury used the word for a patch of sky before it was used for a building.
normal.cn: 罗马占卜先用这个词指一片天空，之后才用于建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid on the ground to mark a square of sky as belonging to a god.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子铺在地上，把一方天空划归某位神明。

abstract.en: Picture a forehead and a temple wall both carrying the same small hollow.
abstract.cn: 想象额头与神庙的墙各有一处相同的小凹。

abstract.en: Picture a library so silent that visitors whisper as if at an altar.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆静得让访客像在祭坛前一样低语。

examples.en: The temple was rebuilt in marble after the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震之后，这座神庙用大理石重建。

examples.en: A small temple stands at the top of the stone stair.
examples.cn: 石阶顶端立着一座小寺庙。

examples.en: The frame's temple snapped where it met the hinge.
examples.cn: 镜架的那条腿在铰链处折断了。

dict_mnemonic.text: templum（划出的神圣空间）→ 神庙；同形词又指额侧平坦处 → 太阳穴

root: 建筑义来自拉丁 templum「划出并祝圣的空间」，后指神庙；太阳穴义来自拉丁 tempora，即「时间」名词的复数，专指额侧；两源不同。英语 temple。templum 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow two paths: a marked-off sacred space becomes a shrine, then a whole class of religious buildings and a metaphor; a separate Latin plural names the forehead, then the glasses arm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分两条线：被划出的神圣空间成为神庙，再扩展为各类宗教建筑与比喻；另一个拉丁复数指额侧，再转指眼镜腿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary drawn around a space, and a hollow at the side of a face that shares the same name.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一处空间画下的界线，以及脸侧一处同名的凹陷。

branches.en: MARKED-OFF SPACE: the shrine and the augur's patch of sky are the same act of setting space apart.
branches.cn: 划出的空间：神庙与占卜官划出的那片天空，是同一个「把空间分开」的动作。

branches.en: MANY FAITHS: translation and new religions apply the word to their own buildings.
branches.cn: 多种信仰：翻译与新宗教把这个词用于自己的建筑。

branches.en: THE UNIQUE SANCTUARY: one building becomes a proper name and a whole covenant.
branches.cn: 唯一的圣所：一座建筑成为专名，也代表一整份盟约。

branches.en: THE FOREHEAD: a separate Latin plural names the head, and glasses borrow it.
branches.cn: 额侧：另一个拉丁复数指头部，眼镜又把它借去。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any revered place can be called a temple of its own craft.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何受敬重的地方都可称为其本行的殿堂。

intro.en: Temple is two words in one shape: a Latin sacred-space noun and a Latin plural for the sides of the head, so the affix list follows both.
intro.cn: temple 是一个词形下的两个词：一个拉丁语「神圣空间」名词与一个指头侧的拉丁语复数，因此词缀清单两条线都跟。

latinIntro.en: Latin templum gave the shrine family, and the plural tempora gave the anatomical family; the verb contemplari grew from templum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 templum 给出神庙一族，复数 tempora 给出解剖一族；动词 contemplari 由 templum 生长出来。

items.example: The augur observed within the templum.
items.exampleCN: 占卜官在划定的圣域内观察。

items.example: The temple stood above the harbour.

items.meaning: the flat side of the forehead
items.example: A pulse beat at his temple.
items.exampleCN: 他的太阳穴处有脉搏跳动。

items.example: The headache sat behind both temples.
items.exampleCN: 头痛压在两侧太阳穴后面。

items.example: The verb began as watching the sky.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词最初指观察天空。

items.meaning: to look at or think about deeply

items.example: The reading room has a temple-like calm.
items.exampleCN: 这间阅览室有一种神庙般的宁静。

latinEntries.structure: tempus, temporis (n., third declension); plural tempora
latinEntries.meaning: time; in the plural, the temples of the head
latinEntries.meaningCN: 时间；复数指头部太阳穴

definition_zh: 时间的；时间先后上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的；（解剖）颞的
definition_en: relating to time or to the order of events, and, in another line of the same spelling, relating to temples of the head or to worldly affairs
core_image: 档案柜的抽屉按年份一层层往下排，同一件事的三份记录落在三个不同的格子里
scene: 档案室里，三份记录同一事件的文件夹按年份排成一列，谁在前谁在后一眼可见。Researchers tracked the temporal order of the three events rather than the distance between them.
sceneCN: 这里指事件在时间上的先后（第 2 个义项：时间先后次序）；句意为研究者追踪三个事件的时间先后，而不是它们之间的空间距离。图中可辨识物件：按年份排列的档案夹、三份记录、年份标签、档案柜。

pos.zh: 时间的；时间上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在时间上；按时间」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「时间性；暂时性」
由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
解剖学中由同一部位名词构成的名称，指颞肌
由表示「在上」的前缀加该解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

senses.title: Relating to time
senses.definition: concerned with time as a dimension
senses.definitionCN: 涉及时间这一维度的
senses.example: The study measures temporal change rather than differences between places.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究测量的是随时间发生的变化，而不是地方之间的差异。
senses.why: The Latin word for time gives this adjective its broadest frame, and most other senses narrow it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「时间」的词给出最宽的框架，其余义项大多是在此之上收窄。

senses.title: Order of events in time
senses.definition: the sequence in which events happen
senses.definitionCN: 事件发生的先后顺序
senses.example: The notes record the temporal order of the symptoms, not their severity.
senses.exampleCN: 记录写的是症状出现的时间先后，而不是轻重。
senses.why: Order needs an axis, and time supplies one; this sense is the everyday core.
senses.whyCN: 次序需要一个轴，时间提供了这个轴，这是最日常的核心义。

senses.title: Time resolution
senses.definition: how finely an instrument or dataset divides time
senses.definitionCN: 仪器或数据集把时间切分的精细程度
senses.example: The camera's temporal resolution is one frame every ten milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这台相机的时间分辨率是每十毫秒一帧。
senses.why: Here time is measured as a grid, so the word marks the fineness of that grid.
senses.whyCN: 这里时间被当成一张网格来量，词于是标出网格的细密程度。

senses.title: The temporal lobe of the brain
senses.definition: the lobe at the side of the head, named from the temples
senses.definitionCN: 位于头侧、因太阳穴部位得名的脑叶
senses.example: The temporal lobe handles much of what we hear and remember.
senses.exampleCN: 颞叶负责我们所听到与记住的很大一部分内容。
senses.why: This sense belongs to a different Latin word, the plural name for the temples of the head.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项属于另一个拉丁词，即「头部太阳穴」的复数形式。

senses.title: Worldly power
senses.definition: authority over worldly affairs as opposed to spiritual authority
senses.definitionCN: 对世俗事务的管辖权，与属灵权力相对
senses.example: The dispute was over temporal power, not over doctrine.
senses.exampleCN: 争论针对的是世俗权力，而不是教义。
senses.why: The church set the authority of this world against the authority of the next, and the word carried the contrast.
senses.whyCN: 教会把此世的权力与彼世的权力对立起来，这个词就承载了这组对照。

senses.title: Earthly and passing
senses.definition: belonging to this world and therefore not lasting
senses.definitionCN: 属于此世、因而不能长久的
senses.example: Monks renounced temporal goods but kept their books.
senses.exampleCN: 修士舍弃尘世的财物，却留下了书。
senses.why: The same axis of time carries a judgement: what is in time will pass.
senses.whyCN: 同一条时间轴带上了判断：凡在时间之中的都会过去。

senses.title: A clause of time
senses.definition: a subordinate clause saying when something happens
senses.definitionCN: 说明某事何时发生的从属分句
senses.example: The sentence opens with a temporal clause introduced by after.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子以表示「之后」的连接词引导的时间从句开头。
senses.why: Grammar names by function, so any clause marking time takes the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 语法按功能命名，凡标出时间的分句都用这个形容词。

senses.title: Temporal scale
senses.definition: the length of time over which something is observed
senses.definitionCN: 观察某事所跨的时间长度
senses.example: Climate and soil form on very different temporal scales.
senses.exampleCN: 气候与土壤在以极为不同的时间尺度形成。
senses.why: Scale is the length of the ruler, and on the time axis the ruler is a span of years.
senses.whyCN: 尺度就是尺子的长度；放在时间轴上，这把尺子就是一段年份。

intro.en: Temporal is two words wearing one shape. The time sense comes from Latin tempus, time, and its adjective temporalis, which also supplied the church's word for worldly affairs. The anatomy sense comes from Latin tempora, the temples of the head, a different word. English merged them in spelling, not in origin.
intro.cn: 这个词其实是两个词穿了同一件外衣。时间义来自拉丁语 tempus「时间」及其形容词，教会又用它指世俗事务。解剖义来自拉丁语 tempora「头部太阳穴」，是另一个词。英语只是在拼写上把它们合在一起，来源并不相同。

items.en: Tempus meant time, with the stem tempor- appearing in all other cases.
items.cn: 这个词意为「时间」，其余各格都用表示「时间」的词干。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to time, and the church used it for what belongs to this world.
items.cn: 该形容词意为「属于时间的」，教会用它指属于此世的事物。

items.en: A separate noun, plural of tempus in the sense of the temples of the head, gave the anatomical word.
items.cn: 另一个名词，即「太阳穴」义的复数，给出了解剖学上的这个词。

items.en: French kept the church contrast between the worldly and the spiritual.
items.cn: 法语保留了教会关于「世俗」与「属灵」的对照。

items.en: English took both senses, and later added the grammatical and scientific uses.
items.cn: 英语把两个义项都吸收进来，后来又加上语法与科学用法。

items.en: Measurement and neuroscience gave the word new compounds; the first dates of those compounds are uncertain.
items.cn: 测量与神经科学又给出新的复合说法；这些说法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the time root or looks close; the second group names time, worldliness and related ideas. The note also contrasts temporal with spatial, and separates the time sense from the anatomy sense.
note.cn: 第一组共享「时间」词根或形近；第二组指时间、世俗及相关概念。这里也把「时间的」与「空间的」对照说清，并分开时间义与解剖义。

entries.definition: Lasting only for a time; the same time root with an ending meaning lasting for a period.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续一段时间；同一时间词根加表示「持续一段」的词尾。

entries.definition: For a limited time only.
entries.definitionCN: 指仅在有限时间内。

entries.definition: The speed of music, from the Italian use of the time word.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐的速度，来自意大利语对「时间」一词的使用。

entries.definition: Existing at the same time; the prefix means with.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时存在的；前缀意为「共同」。

entries.definition: To stall or act evasively in order to gain time.
entries.definitionCN: 指为争取时间而拖延或见风使舵。

entries.definition: Relating to space, the other axis of measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指与空间有关，是测量所用的另一条轴。

entries.definition: Arranged by date, with explicit times attached.
entries.definitionCN: 指按日期排列，并明确标出时间。

entries.definition: Concerned with this world rather than with religion.
entries.definitionCN: 指关心此世而非宗教事务。

entries.definition: Concerned with material life and its affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 指关注物质生活及其事务。

entries.definition: Lasting only a short time and then gone.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续很短时间便消失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the dated file drawers, the framework of the church, the temple-side lobe and the frame rate of a camera.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用按年份排的档案抽屉、教会与世俗的对照、头侧的脑叶以及相机的帧率。

normal.en: Temporal questions ask when, the mirror of spatial questions asking where.
normal.cn: 时间类问题问「什么时候」，正好映照空间类问题的「在哪里」。

normal.en: A temporal clause is a subordinate sentence that answers when.
normal.cn: 时间从句就是回答「何时」的从属句。

normal.en: The temporal lobe sits beside the temples, which is exactly what its Latin name says.
normal.cn: 颞叶位于太阳穴旁，它的拉丁名称说的正是这件事。

normal.en: Temporal power is the church's word for the authority of this world.
normal.cn: 世俗权力是教会用来指此世权威的说法。

normal.en: Temporal scale decides what looks fast and what looks slow.
normal.cn: 时间尺度决定什么看起来快、什么看起来慢。

abstract.en: Time is the axis that makes order visible, and this adjective is the name of that axis.
abstract.cn: 时间是把次序变可见的那条轴，而这个形容词就是这条轴的名字。

abstract.en: Two unrelated Latin nouns ended up with the same English spelling, and only the context tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 两个互不相干的拉丁名词最后拼成了一个英语单词，只能靠上下文分开。

abstract.en: Anything inside time is already leaving, which is why the worldly sense carries a hint of loss.
abstract.cn: 凡在时间之中的都已开始离去，所以世俗义总带一丝失去的意味。

examples.en: The two records differ in temporal order but agree on content.
examples.cn: 这两份记录在时间先后上不同，内容却一致。

examples.en: Temporal power and spiritual authority were once argued in the same courtroom.
examples.cn: 世俗权力与属灵权威曾在一间法庭上被同时争辩。

examples.en: Fossils and languages change on completely different temporal scales.
examples.cn: 化石与语言以完全不同的时间尺度变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦泼若」：先问「时间」什么时候到，再问「尘土」什么时候散，一事一时都记在案上

root: 一支源于拉丁语中表示「时间」的名词及其形容词，教会又引申指「世俗的」；另一支源于拉丁语中表示「头部太阳穴」的复数名词，给出解剖学的「颞的」。两支同形异源，英语只在拼写上合并。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses use two roots: time, its order, its resolution and scale; the anatomy of the temples; worldly power and worldly transience; and the grammar of when.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属两个词根：时间本身、时间次序、时间分辨率与时间尺度；太阳穴部位的解剖；世俗权力与尘世短暂；以及表示「何时」的语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three folders for one event slide into year-labelled drawers, and the order is visible at a glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一事件的三份档案滑进标着年份的抽屉，先后一眼可见。

branches.en: THE AXIS AND ITS ORDER: time as a dimension, then events placed along it.
branches.cn: 轴与轴上的次序：先是时间这一维度，再是沿它摆放的事件。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SPAN: fine resolution at one end, long scale at the other.
branches.cn: 被丈量的跨度：一端是精细分辨率，一端是长尺度。

branches.en: THE TEMPLES' LOBE: a second Latin root hiding under the same spelling.
branches.cn: 太阳穴的脑叶：同一拼写之下藏着第二个拉丁词根。

branches.en: THE WORLD AND ITS PASSING: authority here, and the fact that it fades.
branches.cn: 此世与其消逝：这里的权力，以及它终将褪去。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE OF WHEN: grammar marking time in a sentence.
branches.cn: 「何时」从句：语法在句中标出时间。

intro.en: Temporal is a Latin time noun with an adjective ending; its family covers lasting for a time, the musical tempo, and the anatomy of the temples.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「时间」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖「暂时的」、音乐的速度，以及太阳穴的解剖。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus and its stem tempor- supply the time line, while the plural tempora supplies the anatomy line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「时间」及其词干提供时间这一线，而复数形式「太阳穴」提供解剖这一线。

items.example: The source of the time sense.
The stem seen in temporal and temporary.
items.exampleCN: 见于「时间的」与「暂时的」两词。
它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: A separate word behind the anatomy sense.
items.exampleCN: 解剖义背后是另一个词。

items.example: It marks both senses as adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 它把两个义项都标为形容词。

items.example: It forms temporary, lasting for a time.

由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
由表示「在上」的前缀加解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

definition_zh: 临时的；暂时的；短期的；非永久的；临时工（名词，常用复数）
definition_en: lasting only for a limited time; intended to be used or kept for a short period
core_image: 工地入口立着一块临时围挡，风一吹就晃，却已经立了三年
scene: 搬进新家前，他们先住进一间小公寓。They stayed in a temporary flat while the new house was being painted, and moved out as soon as the work was finished.
sceneCN: 这里 temporary 是「临时的、暂时的」（第 1 个义项：只持续有限时间）；句意：新房刷漆期间他们住在一间临时公寓，一完工就搬走了。图中可辨识物件：简易公寓、纸箱、未拆封的家具、装修中的新房、搬家货车。

pos.zh: 临时工；临时事物（常用复数）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）

senses.title: Lasting a short time
senses.definition: lasting only for a limited period, not forever
senses.definitionCN: 只持续有限时段，不会永远
senses.example: They found temporary shelter under a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在桥下找到临时遮蔽。
senses.why: Temporary is defined by an end. It does not say how short the period is, only that a limit exists and is expected to arrive.
senses.whyCN: temporary 由“终点”定义。它不说时段多短，只说存在一个被预期会到来的界限。

senses.title: Not permanent
senses.definition: not intended to last or to be final
senses.definitionCN: 不打算长久保留或成为最终状态
senses.example: The agreement is temporary and will be reviewed.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议是暂时的，将会复审。
senses.why: The word often carries a promise or a warning: this state is provisional, so do not build your life on it, or do not despair of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常带承诺或警告：此状态是暂定的，故不要把生活建在其上，也别为它绝望。

senses.title: Of a short-term job
senses.definition: of work or a post that ends after a fixed period
senses.definitionCN: 有固定期限、到期即止的工作或职位
senses.example: She took a temporary job for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了份暑期临时工作。
senses.why: Labour markets use temporary as a category: the contract has an end date, and with it fewer rights and less security.
senses.whyCN: 劳动力市场把 temporary 当作类别：合同有终止日，随之而来的是更少的权利与保障。

senses.title: Of short-term lodging
senses.definition: of accommodation used until something permanent is available
senses.definitionCN: 在永久住处可用之前使用的住所
senses.example: The family stayed in temporary housing after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾后这家人住进临时住房。
senses.why: Housing makes the word concrete: a roof that is known to be borrowed, often provided by an agency or a friend, and marked by boxes not yet unpacked.
senses.whyCN: 住房把词变具体：一个明知是借来的屋顶，常由机构或朋友提供，以尚未拆封的纸箱为标志。

senses.title: A temporary worker (noun)
senses.definition: a person employed for a limited period, often through an agency
senses.definitionCN: 受雇有限期限的人，常经中介
senses.example: The hospital hired temporaries for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 医院为冬季雇了临时工。
senses.why: The noun turns the adjective into a person. 'Temps' is the clipped, everyday form; the plural temporaries is more formal.
senses.whyCN: 名词把形容词变成人。口语缩略为 temp；复数 temporaries 更正式。

senses.title: A stopgap measure
senses.definition: an arrangement used to solve a problem until a better one is possible
senses.definitionCN: 在更好办法出现前用来解决问题的安排
senses.example: The ban is a temporary measure, not a policy.
senses.exampleCN: 该禁令是权宜之计，而非政策。
senses.why: A temporary measure admits its own inadequacy. It buys time, and the honest ones say so rather than pretending to be final.
senses.whyCN: 权宜之计承认自身不足。它买时间，诚实者会明说，而不假装是最终方案。

senses.title: A temporary file
senses.definition: a computer file created for a short task and deleted later
senses.definitionCN: 为短期任务创建、随后删除的计算机文件
senses.example: The installer left temporary files on the disk.
senses.exampleCN: 安装程序在磁盘上留下了临时文件。
senses.why: Computing literalises the word: the file exists only while a process runs, and its deletion is part of its design.
senses.whyCN: 计算把词字面化：文件只在进程运行时存在，其删除是设计的一部分。

senses.title: A short stay
senses.definition: a visit or residence lasting only a while
senses.definitionCN: 只持续一段时日的访问或居住
senses.example: He made a temporary stay in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城里作短期停留。
senses.why: Travel and diplomacy use the word for presence that is explicitly not settlement. The visitor is in place but not of it.
senses.whyCN: 旅行与外交用该词指明确不落户的存在。访客在此地，却不属于此地。

senses.title: A passing setback
senses.definition: a difficulty expected to improve with time
senses.definitionCN: 预期随时间好转的困难
senses.example: The loss was a temporary setback, not a collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 这次亏损是暂时挫折，不是崩溃。
senses.why: Applied to feelings and fortunes, temporary is consolation: it reframes a present pain as a phase with an exit.
senses.whyCN: 用于情绪与境遇时，temporary 是安慰：它把当下的痛重新框定为有出口的阶段。

intro.en: Temporary comes from Latin temporarius, 'of a time, lasting for a time', from tempus 'time' (genitive temporis). English took it in the sixteenth century. The deeper origin of tempus is uncertain; it is often connected with a root meaning 'to stretch or span'.
intro.cn: temporary 出自拉丁语 temporarius“某段时间的、暂时的”，源于 tempus“时间”（属格 temporis）。英语十六世纪借入。tempus 的更早来源不确定，常与表示“伸展、跨度”的词根相连。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in English in the sense 'lasting only for a time'.
items.cn: 该形容词最早记录于十六世纪四十年代，意为“只持续一段时间的”。

items.en: temporarius means 'of time, belonging to a time, transient', from tempus 'time, season'.
items.cn: temporarius 意为“时间的、属于某时段的、短暂的”，出自 tempus“时间、季节”。

items.en: tempus has the genitive temporis, which is why temporary has an r where the base word seems to lack one.
items.cn: tempus 的属格是 temporis，故 temporary 在词基看似没有 r 的地方出现了一个 r。

items.en: The Indo-European origin of tempus is disputed. A connection with a root meaning 'to stretch, span' is often proposed but not certain.
items.cn: tempus 的印欧来源有争议。常有人提出与表示“伸展、跨度”的词根相关，但并不确定。

items.en: Legal and religious writing spread the word: temporal goods are of this world, temporary arrangements last only a while.
items.cn: 十六世纪法律与宗教写作推广该词：temporal 之物属于此世，temporary 安排只维持一时。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from temp work and temporary housing to temporary files, all sharing an expected end point.
items.cn: 现代用法从临时工作、临时住房到临时文件，皆共享一个预期终点。

note.en: The first group is the tempus family, where r-forms and plain forms alternate; the second is words for shortness of duration, each with a different tone.
note.cn: 第一组是 tempus 词族，r 形式与无 r 形式交替；第二组是表示时短的其他词，语气各异。

entries.definition: for a limited time only.
entries.definitionCN: 只限一段时间地。

entries.definition: the quality of lasting only a while.
entries.definitionCN: 只持续一时的性质。

entries.definition: relating to time, or to worldly rather than spiritual matters.
entries.definitionCN: 关于时间的；世俗的（非属灵的）。

entries.definition: lasting only a very short time and passing quickly. It is more literary and more absolute than temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 只持续极短时间并迅速消逝。比 temporary 更文学、更绝对。

entries.definition: used or done between two points in time, especially between two official arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 在两个时点之间、尤在两个正式安排之间使用或做的。

entries.definition: arranged for the present but likely to be changed. It stresses conditionality rather than duration.
entries.definitionCN: 为当下安排但很可能被改。强调条件性而非时长。

normalIntro.en: Real links: tempus/temporis, the r in the English word, the temp-work sense, and the contrast with permanent.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tempus 与 temporis、英语词中的 r、临时工作义，以及同 permanent 的对照。

normal.en: Tempus means time, and its genitive is temporis. That hidden r is why English has temporary.
normal.cn: tempus 意为时间，属格是 temporis。那个藏起来的 r 正是英语 temporary 的来源。

normal.en: Temporary is defined by an end: it does not say how short, only that a stop is expected.
normal.cn: temporary 由终点定义：它不说多短，只说预期会停。

normal.en: A temp job has an end date written into the contract; the word is a legal fact, not just a feeling.
normal.cn: 临时工作的合同里写着终止日；这个词是法律事实，不只是感觉。

normal.en: A temporary file exists only while a process runs; deleting it is part of its design.
normal.cn: 临时文件只在进程运行时存在；删除它是设计的一部分。

normal.en: Temporary vs permanent: one expects an exit, the other expects to remain.
normal.cn: temporary 与 permanent：前者预期出口，后者预期留下。

abstract.en: The temporary is not less real; it is real with a clock attached.
abstract.cn: 临时之物并非不那么真实；它是被系上时钟的真实。

abstract.en: Calling something temporary is a political act: it can make an injustice easier to bear or harder to oppose.
abstract.cn: 把某物称为临时，是一种政治行为：它能让不义更易忍受，也能让它更难被反对。

abstract.en: All arrangements are temporary at some scale; the word only makes the scale visible.
abstract.cn: 一切安排在某个尺度上都是临时的；这个词只是让尺度显现。

examples.en: The museum is closed for temporary repairs.
examples.cn: 博物馆因临时维修闭馆。

examples.en: He took a temporary position at the bank.
examples.cn: 他在银行做了一份临时职位。

examples.en: The decline in sales proved temporary.
examples.cn: 销售下滑被证明是暂时的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摊破若瑞”——摊子破了也别急，若天降祥瑞，很快就能换新的 → temporary 临时的

root: 拉丁语 temporarius“某段时间的、短暂的”，出自 tempus“时间、季节”（属格 temporis）；tempus 的印欧来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of temporary, all marked by an expected end. The end may be a date on a contract, the completion of a house, the closing of a file, or the passing of a mood.
sensesIntro.cn: temporary 的九个义项都以“预期终点”为标记。终点可以是合同日期、房子装完、文件关闭，或情绪过去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a temporary fence that is expected to come down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道预期会被拆掉的临时围挡。

branches.en: DURATION: the word measures a limited span and denies permanence.
branches.cn: 时长：衡量有限跨度，并否认永久。

branches.en: LIFE ARRANGEMENTS: jobs, housing, and the people who fill them are all marked by an end date.
branches.cn: 生活安排：工作、住房与填充其中的人，都带终止日。

branches.en: THE STOPGAP: measures and setbacks are framed as phases with an exit.
branches.cn: 权宜：措施与挫折被框定为有出口的阶段。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the file exists only while needed, and deletion is designed in.
branches.cn: 计算：文件只在需要时存在，删除是设计的一部分。

branches.en: PRESENCE: a short stay is presence without settlement.
branches.cn: 在场：短期停留是“在场而不落户”。

intro.en: Temporary is a Latin adjective in -arius built on the tempus/tempor- stem. English derives -ly and -ness, while the same stem gives temporal, contemporary, tempo, and tempest.
intro.cn: temporary 是建于 tempus/tempor- 词干的拉丁 -arius 形容词。英语派生 -ly 与 -ness，同一词干给出 temporal、contemporary、tempo、tempest。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus 'time' has the stem tempor-, which supplies temporarius 'lasting a time'. The family includes temporal (of time), contemporary (of the same time), and tempo (time in music). The ultimate origin of tempus is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tempus“时间”的词干为 tempor-，生成 temporarius“持续一段时间的”。词族含 temporal（时间的）、contemporary（同时代的）、tempo（音乐的时间）。tempus 的最终来源不确定。
