临时性；暂时性（-ness 名词）
时间的；世俗的（-al 形容词）
节拍；速度（同词干，经意大利语）

items.meaning: to act for the moment; to delay
items.meaningCN: 顺应时势；拖延（同词干动词）

definition_zh: 诱惑；引诱；诱惑物
definition_en: a strong wish or urge to do something, especially something wrong or unwise
core_image: 一根挂在眼前的胡萝卜，越忍越香
scene: 减肥的人站在甜品店橱窗前，玻璃把香气都递了过来。She resisted the temptation of the chocolate cake.
sceneCN: 这里 temptation 是「诱惑」（第 1 个义项：做不该做之事的强烈欲念）；句意：她抵挡住了巧克力蛋糕的诱惑。

derivatives.zh: 引诱；怂恿（动词原形，-ation 为名词后缀）
诱人的（现在分词转形容词）
诱惑者（动词加表人后缀）

senses.title: An urge to do something wrong or unwise
senses.definition: a strong wish to do something that one should not do
senses.definitionCN: 想做不该做之事的强烈愿望
senses.example: He could not resist the temptation to check his phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他忍不住想看手机。
senses.why: The image is bait: an outside pull that tests the will, as if something were dangled before you.
senses.whyCN: 意象是诱饵：一种试探意志的外来拉力，仿佛有什么东西在你眼前晃。

senses.title: Something that attracts strongly
senses.definition: a thing or person that makes someone want it
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生强烈欲望的事物或人
senses.example: The dessert tray was a temptation we could not refuse.
senses.exampleCN: 甜品托盘是我们无法拒绝的诱惑。
senses.why: The pull becomes a thing you can point at: the bait itself is named temptation.
senses.whyCN: 拉力被落成实物：诱饵本身就被叫作 temptation。

senses.title: A test of character in religious use
senses.definition: in religious language, a trial that tests faith or obedience
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语境中考验信仰或顺从的试炼
senses.example: The prayer asks to be led away from temptation.
senses.exampleCN: 祷文祈求远离试探。
senses.why: Here the bait is set deliberately, not by desire but by the tester, making the pull a trial.
senses.whyCN: 这里的诱饵是被刻意放置的：设局者并非欲望本身，试探成了考验。

intro.en: Temptation comes from Latin temptare or tentare, to test, try, or stretch toward, through Latin temptatio and Old French.
intro.cn: temptation 源自拉丁语 temptare/tentare「试探、尝试、向…伸去」，经 temptatio 与古法语传入英语。

items.en: Temptare meant to feel after, test, or try; some scholars link it with tendere, to stretch toward.
items.cn: temptare 意为试探、尝试；有学者将其与 tendere「朝…伸展」相联。

items.en: Temptatio named a trial or an attempt, later a testing of the soul.
items.cn: temptatio 指试炼或尝试，后指对灵魂的考验。

items.en: Old French temptacion carried the religious trial sense into medieval life.
items.cn: 古法语 temptacion 带着宗教试炼义进入中世纪生活。

items.en: English borrowed the word with both senses: testing and luring.
items.cn: 英语借入该词时兼有两义：考验与诱引。

items.en: The everyday lure sense prevailed; the trial sense survives mainly in religious language.
items.cn: 日常「诱引」义占了上风；「试炼」义主要存活于宗教语言。

note.en: Temptation is compared with its own verb family and with words for desire and pull.
note.cn: 把 temptation 与其动词词族，以及表示欲望与拉力的词对比。

entries.definition: to try to make someone do something
entries.definitionCN: 引诱；怂恿

entries.definition: attractive, making you want it
entries.definitionCN: 诱人的

entries.definition: to try; a try itself
entries.definitionCN: 尝试；企图，保留「试」的拉丁义

entries.definition: the quality of being powerfully attractive
entries.definitionCN: 魅力；吸引力

entries.definition: a strong inner wish
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的内在冲动

entries.definition: a thing that attracts, like bait
entries.definitionCN: 诱饵；吸引物

normalIntro.en: Real links: temptare to test, attempt as a cousin, the bait image, and resist or give in.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：temptare「试探」、attempt 这个表亲、诱饵意象、resist 与 give in。

normal.en: Temptare means to test; every temptation tests your will.
normal.cn: temptare 意为试探；每次诱惑都在测你的意志。

normal.en: Attempt keeps the old test sense: an attempt is a try.
normal.cn: attempt 保留古义「试」：attempt 就是尝试。

normal.en: The carrot picture: temptation is a pull from outside.
normal.cn: 胡萝卜画面：诱惑是来自外面的拉力。

normal.en: Resist the temptation, or give in to it: two verbs of one tug-of-war.
normal.cn: resist 与 give in：同一场拔河的两个动词。

normal.en: Tempting food is bait shaped like dinner.
normal.cn: 诱人的食物就是做成晚餐形状的诱饵。

abstract.en: Every temptation is a small experiment on your will.
abstract.cn: 每次诱惑都是对你意志的小实验。

abstract.en: The bait smells sweetest exactly when the will is weakest.
abstract.cn: 意志最弱时，诱饵正香。

abstract.en: Desire speaks first; character answers later.
abstract.cn: 欲望先开口，品格后作答。

examples.en: The smell of fresh bread was too much temptation for him.
examples.cn: 新鲜面包的香气对他诱惑太大。

examples.en: Resist the temptation to reply in anger.
examples.cn: 抵制怒气回复的冲动。

examples.en: A free holiday offer is a temptation few can refuse.
examples.cn: 免费度假的提议很少有人能拒绝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「탬ptation」——念作「疼劈-too-申」：疼也要劈开那块蛋糕，申手去拿 → temptation 诱惑

root: 拉丁语 temptare「试探、尝试」（一说与 tendere「伸展」相关）→ temptatio「试炼、诱引」→ 古法语 temptacion → 英语 temptation。

sensesIntro.en: From a trial of the soul to the everyday pull of cake, phone and bargain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对灵魂的试炼，到蛋糕、手机与折扣的日常拉力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bait dangled before the will.
core.cn: 核心意象：悬在意志面前的诱饵。

branches.en: The pull is felt, the bait unseen.
branches.cn: 拉力被感到，诱饵未被看见。

branches.en: The bait itself is named and priced.
branches.cn: 诱饵本身被点名标价。

branches.en: When the tester is divine, the trial is holy.
branches.cn: 当设局者是神，试炼便成圣课。

branches.en: Two verbs hang on it: resist and yield.
branches.cn: 两个动词挂在其上：抵制与屈服。

branches.en: Every urge is a test wearing a costume.
branches.cn: 每个冲动都是化了装的试验。

intro.en: Temptation belongs to the Latin temptare family with tempt, attempt and tempting.
intro.cn: temptation 属拉丁 temptare 词族，同族有 tempt、attempt、tempting。

latinIntro.en: Latin temptare, to test or try, possibly related to tendere, to stretch toward; the link is proposed, not certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 temptare「试探」，可能与 tendere「朝…伸展」相关；此说未确证。

definition_zh: 承租人；租户；保有者；按份共有人
definition_en: a person who holds or occupies land or buildings that belong to someone else
core_image: 一把钥匙握在手里：房子不属于他，却由他持有和使用
scene: 房东把钥匙交给新住户，双方在租约上签字。The landlord handed the keys to the tenant and both signed the lease.
sceneCN: 这里 tenant 是「承租人」（第 1 个义项：按租约持有并使用他人房产的人）；句意：房东把钥匙交给承租人，双方在租约上签字。

collocations.zh: 随意租户；可随时终止租约的租户

derivatives.zh: 由 tenant 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「租赁；租期；保有」
由 tenant 加 -able 构成，义为「可出租的；适宜租住的」
由 tenant 加集合后缀 -ry 构成，义为「全体租户；佃农群体」

senses.title: One who holds a lease
senses.definition: a person or business that holds a lease of land or premises from a landlord
senses.definitionCN: 从房东处取得土地或房屋租约的人或企业
senses.example: The tenant agreed to pay rent monthly.
senses.exampleCN: 承租人同意按月支付租金。
senses.why: The Old French participle meant a holder, so a tenant is literally the one holding the leased property.
senses.whyCN: 古法语分词本义为「持有者」，所以承租人字面上就是持有租赁物的一方，这一层「持有」正是词根 tenere 的直传。

senses.title: An occupier without a written lease
senses.definition: a person who occupies premises under an informal or periodic arrangement, such as a tenancy at will
senses.definitionCN: 以非正式或周期性安排占用房屋的人，如随意租户
senses.example: A tenant at will may leave after giving reasonable notice.
senses.exampleCN: 随意租户可以在发出合理通知后搬离。
senses.why: Holding can be practical rather than contractual, so the word also names whoever occupies the space.
senses.whyCN: 「持有」可以只是实际占用而不必有合同，于是这个词也用来指任何占着这处房产的人，义项由此从租约扩展到占用。

senses.title: A co-owner with an undivided share
senses.definition: one of two or more owners who each hold an undivided share of the same property, as in a tenancy in common
senses.definitionCN: 两人或多人各自持有同一房产不可分割份额的共有人，如按份共有中的共有人
senses.example: Each tenant in common may sell an undivided share.
senses.exampleCN: 每一位按份共有人都可以出售自己那份不可分割的份额。
senses.why: The holding root extends to any holder of a share, so property law uses tenant for co-owners too.
senses.whyCN: 「持有」的词根可以扩展到任何持有份额的人，所以物权法也用 tenant 指共有人，这是从「持有实物」到「持有份额」的抽象化。

intro.en: Tenant comes from Latin tenere, to hold, through the Old French participle tenant, the holding one.
intro.cn: tenant 来自拉丁语 tenere（持有），经古法语分词 tenant（持有着的）进入英语。

items.en: Tenere means to hold, to keep, or to keep in the hand.
items.cn: tenere 意为握持、保有、握在手中。

items.en: The participle tenens, tenentis describes the one who holds.
items.cn: 分词 tenens、tenentis 描述「正持有的人」。

items.en: The verb tenir, to hold, yields the participle tenant.
items.cn: 动词 tenir（持有）产生分词 tenant。

items.en: Tenant names the person who holds lands of a lord by some tenure.
items.cn: 中古英语 tenant 指按某种保有方式持有领主土地的人。

items.en: Tenant becomes the standard word for a lessee, and for a co-owner in a tenancy in common.
items.cn: 现代英语中 tenant 成为承租人的标准说法，也指按份共有中的共有人。

note.en: Tenant belongs to the Latin hold family and sits beside lease and occupancy words.
note.cn: tenant 属于拉丁语「持有」词族，与租赁和占用义场的词相邻。

entries.definition: the holding of land or premises under a lease
entries.definitionCN: 依租约对土地或房屋的持有；租赁；租期

entries.definition: a rented dwelling or a building divided into rented flats
entries.definitionCN: 出租住宅；分成若干出租单元的老式楼宇

entries.definition: the way in which land or an office is held
entries.definitionCN: 土地或职位的保有方式；任期

entries.definition: the party who holds a lease and pays rent
entries.definitionCN: 持有租约并支付租金的一方；承租方

entries.definition: a person who rents a room in a house owned by someone else
entries.definitionCN: 在他人所有的住宅里租住一间房的人；房客

entries.definition: a person who is in occupation of a place
entries.definitionCN: 占用或使用某处场所的人；占用人

normalIntro.en: Tenant grows from a Latin verb of holding: the person who holds land rather than owns it.
normalIntro.cn: tenant 长自一个表示「持有」的拉丁语动词：持有土地而不是拥有土地的人。

normal.en: Ten- comes from tenere, to hold, and -ant marks the person who does it.
normal.cn: ten- 来自 tenere（持有），-ant 标记做这件事的人。

normal.en: Tenancy is the holding itself, and tenure is the way it is held.
normal.cn: tenancy 是持有这件事本身，tenure 是持有的方式。

normal.en: A tenant at will holds with no fixed term and may leave on notice.
normal.cn: 「tenant at will」是没有固定期限、通知后即可离开的租户。

normal.en: A tenant in common holds an undivided share together with others.
normal.cn: 「tenant in common」与他人共同持有一份不可分割的份额。

normal.en: Landlord and tenant are the two parties named in a lease.
normal.cn: 「landlord and tenant」就是租约里写明的两方。

abstract.en: A hand closes around a key to a flat that belongs to another person.
abstract.cn: 一只手握住一套不属于自己的房子的钥匙，画面突出「持有而不拥有」。

abstract.en: A family lives month to month in a house with no written contract.
abstract.cn: 一家人按月住在一栋没有书面合同的房子里，对应无固定期限的占用人。

abstract.en: Two people each hold one half of the same house, neither owning a fixed room.
abstract.cn: 两个人各握同一栋房子的一半，谁都没有固定的一间房，对应按份共有。

examples.en: The tenant must pay the rent on the first day of each month.
examples.cn: 承租人必须在每月第一天支付租金。

examples.en: A landlord may not enter the premises without notice to the tenant.
examples.cn: 房东未通知承租人不得进入房屋。

examples.en: Each tenant in common may sell an undivided share of the property.
examples.cn: 每位按份共有人都可以出售自己那份不可分割的房产份额。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ten + ant」——十只蚂蚁搬进别人的房子住下不走，就成了租户；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（持有、握持）→ 分词 tenens（持有者）→ 古法语 tenir 的分词 tenant（持有者）→ 英语 tenant，核心义「持有他人土地或房产的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Tenant starts as the leaseholder, widens to any occupier of premises, and finally covers a co-owner who holds an undivided share.
sensesIntro.cn: tenant 先指按租约持有房产的承租人，再扩展到没有书面租约的占用人，最后指按份共有中持有份额的共有人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key held in the hand of someone who does not own the building.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙握在不拥有这栋房子的人手里。

branches.en: The leaseholder is the core legal sense of the word.
branches.cn: 承租人这个词的核心法律义项，就是按租约持有房产的一方。

branches.en: Occupation without a written lease is the looser, practical sense.
branches.cn: 没有书面租约的占用，是更宽松、更贴近实际的一层义项。

branches.en: A co-owner holding an undivided share is the property-law extension.
branches.cn: 持有不可分割份额的共有人，是物权法方向的延伸义项。

branches.en: Both senses describe someone in possession of premises owned by another.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都描述「占着别人名下房产」的人，只是有无合同不同。

branches.en: Both rest on holding rather than owning, which is the shared core.
branches.cn: 两者都落在「持有」而不是「所有」上，这正是共同的核心。

intro.en: Tenant is built on the Latin hold family, with tenere, tenens, tenancy, tenure, and tenement around it.
intro.cn: tenant 建在拉丁语「持有」词族上，周围有 tenere、tenens、tenancy、tenure 与 tenement。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold, and its participle tenens names the one who holds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 意为持有，其分词 tenens 指持有者。

items.example: Tenere is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: tenere 是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The participle supplies the image of a holder.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词提供了「持有者」的意象。

items.example: Tenir carries the Latin verb into French.
items.exampleCN: tenir 把拉丁语动词带进法语。

items.example: The suffix -ant turns a participle into a person noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 把分词变成指人的名词。

items.example: Tenant is the everyday legal noun.
items.exampleCN: tenant 是日常使用的法律名词。
tenancy 指持有租赁房产这件事。

items.meaning: the way land or office is held
items.example: Tenure describes how the holding is held.
items.exampleCN: tenure 描述持有采取的方式。

items.meaning: a rented dwelling or divided building
items.example: Tenement keeps the older sense of a holding.
items.exampleCN: tenement 保留「保有物」的旧义。

items.example: Tenantable describes housing fit for tenants.
items.exampleCN: tenantable 描述适合租户居住的房屋。

items.example: Tenantless means standing empty of renters.
items.exampleCN: tenantless 表示没有租户入住。

definition_zh: 倾向；有…趋势；趋向；照料；照看；管理；在酒吧当班；放牧；（古）侍候
definition_en: to be likely to do something or to move in a certain direction; to take care of someone or something
core_image: 水往低处流，而牧人低头跟着羊群往坡下走
scene: 每到冬天，他的咳嗽就更厉害。Every winter his cough tends to get worse, and the doctor says the cold air is the cause.
sceneCN: 这里 tend 是「倾向于、有…趋势」（第 1 个义项：经常如此或很可能如此）；句意：每年冬天他的咳嗽都倾向于加重，医生说是冷空气刺激。图中可辨识物件：病历、冬季窗景、雾化器、围巾、医生的听诊器。

pos.zh: 倾向；趋向；照料；照看；管理；当班

derivatives.zh: 照料者；温柔的（同根近亲，义已分化）

senses.title: Be likely to do something
senses.definition: to be likely to do or be something, as a regular pattern
senses.definitionCN: 经常如此或很可能如此
senses.example: People tend to ignore warnings they hear too often.
senses.exampleCN: 人们倾向于忽略听太多的警告。
senses.why: Tendere means 'to stretch'. The modern sense pictures behaviour stretched toward one outcome: the pattern leans, and prediction follows the lean.
senses.whyCN: tendere 意为“伸展”。现代义把行为想象为朝某个结果伸展：模式倾斜，预测随倾斜而来。

senses.title: Take care of someone
senses.definition: to look after a person, especially one who is ill or young
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人，尤指病者或幼者
senses.example: Nurses tended the wounded through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 护士整夜照料伤员。
senses.why: This sense has a different parent: it is a shortened form of attend, 'to direct one's mind to'. Care is attention made practical.
senses.whyCN: 此义另有来源：它是 attend“把心思朝向”的缩略。照料是“注意”被付诸实践。

senses.title: Move in a direction
senses.definition: to move or point toward a place or state
senses.definitionCN: 朝某处或某状态移动、指向
senses.example: The path tends toward the river.
senses.exampleCN: 小径趋向河边。
senses.why: The spatial sense is the most literal: a line or a road stretches in a direction. Inclination in behaviour is this stretching made mental.
senses.whyCN: 空间义最字面：一条线或路朝某方向伸展。行为上的倾向，就是这种伸展被心智化。

senses.title: Have an inclination of opinion
senses.definition: to be inclined to hold a view or favour an option
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于持有某观点或支持某选项
senses.example: The committee tends toward a compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于妥协。
senses.why: Opinions also lean. The verb lets a speaker report a drift without claiming a fixed position: the group is not there yet, but it is tending there.
senses.whyCN: 观点也会倾斜。动词让说话者报告一种漂移而不宣称固定立场：群体尚未到达，但正朝那里去。

senses.title: Look after a fire or machine
senses.definition: to keep a fire, machine, or process working properly
senses.definitionCN: 使炉火、机器或过程正常运转
senses.example: He tended the furnace all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他整夜照看炉子。
senses.why: Tending a fire is maintenance as attention: add fuel, watch the draft, respond to changes. The cared-for object is not alive, but it needs vigilance.
senses.whyCN: 照看炉火是“注意”式的维护：添燃料、看通风、应对变化。被照看之物并非活物，却需要警觉。

senses.title: Serve in a bar
senses.definition: to work behind a bar, serving drinks
senses.definitionCN: 在吧台后工作、供应饮品
senses.example: She tends bar on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 她周末在酒吧当班。
senses.why: American English uses tend for a workplace one keeps running. The bartender tends the bar as a shepherd tends a flock: presence plus upkeep.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语用 tend 指维持一个工作场所运转。酒吧侍者 tend 吧台，如牧人 tend 羊群：在场加维护。

senses.title: Herd animals
senses.definition: to watch over animals as they graze
senses.definitionCN: 看管吃草的牲畜
senses.example: A boy tended the goats on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 一个男孩在山坡上放羊。
senses.why: Herding is the oldest care sense: the animals move, and the herder's attention moves with them, keeping them from straying.
senses.whyCN: 放牧是最古老的照料义：牲畜移动，牧人的注意力随之前移，防止它们走失。

senses.title: Attend or wait upon (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to attend on a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：随侍地位高者
senses.example: The squire tended his lord.
senses.exampleCN: 侍从随侍他的领主。
senses.why: This is the attend branch in its full feudal form: standing ready, mind directed toward the master's needs. Modern care kept the service and dropped the rank.
senses.whyCN: 这是 attend 一支的完整封建形态：立于一旁待命，心思朝向主人的需要。现代“照料”保留服侍，丢掉等级。

senses.title: Converge on a result
senses.definition: of numbers or processes, to approach a limit or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 数字或过程逼近某一极限或结果
senses.example: Under these rules, costs tend toward zero.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些规则下，成本趋于零。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the spatial lean for convergence: a sequence stretches toward a limit it may never reach exactly.
senses.whyCN: 数学用空间倾斜表示收敛：序列朝一个可能永远不能精确到达的极限伸展。

intro.en: English has two tend verbs that now look alike. The 'incline' tend comes from Old French tendre, Latin tendere 'to stretch'. The 'care for' tend is a shortened form of attend, from Old French atendre, Latin attendere 'to give heed'. They merged in spelling but not in origin.
intro.cn: 英语有两个现已形似的 tend 动词。“倾向”的 tend 出自古法语 tendre、拉丁 tendere“伸展”；“照料”的 tend 是 attend 的缩略，出自古法语 atendre、拉丁 attendere“留心”。它们在拼写上合并，来源却不同。

items.en: The 'stretch, incline' verb enters English from Old French tendre, used of movement and direction.
items.cn: “伸展、倾向”动词十三世纪自法语 tendre 进入英语，用于移动与方向。

items.en: tendere means 'to stretch, extend, direct'. Its past participle tensus gives tense and tension.
items.cn: tendere 意为“伸展、延伸、指向”。其过去分词 tensus 生成 tense 与 tension。

items.en: tendere is traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch', the same root behind tendon and the ten- of intend and extend.
items.cn: tendere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”，同一词根见于 tendon，以及 intend、extend 中的 ten-。

items.en: The 'care for' sense comes from attend, 'to direct the mind to', later shortened to tend in everyday use.
items.cn: “照料”义出自 attend“把心思朝向”，后在日常使用中缩略为 tend。

items.en: attendere is ad- 'to' plus tendere 'stretch': to stretch one's mind toward something. So care and inclination are distant cousins after all.
items.cn: attendere 是 ad-“朝向”加 tendere“伸展”：把心思朝某物伸去。故“照料”与“倾向”终究是远亲。

items.en: Modern English keeps both: tend to do (incline) and tend a fire (care for). Context, not spelling, tells them apart.
items.cn: 现代英语两者皆存：tend to do（倾向）与 tend a fire（照看）。区分靠语境，不靠拼写。

note.en: The first group is the tend family and its look-alikes; the second is verbs that share either the leaning or the caring sense.
note.cn: 第一组是 tend 词族与形近词；第二组是共享“倾斜”或“照料”义的动词。

entries.definition: a regular inclination to behave in a certain way.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行事的经常性倾向。

entries.definition: expressing a strong biased point of view. It comes from German Tendenz, not directly from English tend.
entries.definitionCN: 表达强烈偏见的。出自德语 Tendenz，并非直接来自英语 tend。

entries.definition: looking after; the act of caring for.
entries.definitionCN: 照看；照料的行为。

entries.definition: to lean or be disposed toward something. It is more formal and more spatial than tend.
entries.definitionCN: 向某物倾斜或有意向。比 tend 更正式、更空间化。

entries.definition: to look after someone's needs. It is the plain phrase for the 'tend' care sense.
entries.definitionCN: 照看某人的需要。是“照料”义的朴素说法。

entries.definition: to be drawn toward something as if by gravity. It stresses attraction rather than habit.
entries.definitionCN: 如受重力吸引般趋向某物。强调吸引而非习惯。

normalIntro.en: Real links: tendere 'stretch', attend shortened to tend, the tense/tension family, and the two-verb history.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tendere“伸展”、attend 缩略为 tend、tense 与 tension 词族，以及“双动词”历史。

normal.en: Tendere means 'stretch'. Behaviour tends when it stretches toward one outcome rather than another.
normal.cn: tendere 意为“伸展”。行为 tend，就是朝某个结果而非另一个伸展。

normal.en: The care sense is attend shortened: to tend a patient is to stretch your attention toward them.
normal.cn: 照料义是 attend 的缩略：tend 病人，就是把注意力朝他们伸去。

normal.en: Tend, tense, tension, tendon all go back to stretching. A tendon is a stretched cord.
normal.cn: tend、tense、tension、tendon 都回到“伸展”。肌腱就是一根被拉紧的索。

normal.en: Tend to do = habit leans; tend a fire = attention stays. Context decides which verb you met.
normal.cn: tend to do 是习惯倾斜；tend a fire 是注意力留守。语境决定你遇到哪一个。

normal.en: Intend and extend hide the same ten-: stretching the mind toward, or stretching out.
normal.cn: intend 与 extend 藏着同一个 ten-：把心思伸向，或向外伸展。

abstract.en: A tendency is a future written into the present as a slope; tend names the slope without promising the destination.
abstract.cn: 倾向是写进当下的未来，形如斜坡；tend 命名坡度，却不承诺终点。

abstract.en: Care and inclination meet in attention: both are a stretching of the self toward something beyond it.
abstract.cn: 照料与倾向在“注意”处相遇：两者都是自我朝外物的伸展。

abstract.en: What we tend grows; what we merely intend does not. The hand matters more than the plan.
abstract.cn: 我们所照料的东西会生长；仅仅所意图的不会。手比计划更重要。

examples.en: Prices tend to rise before the holiday.
examples.cn: 节前价格往往上涨。

examples.en: A nurse tended him through the night.
examples.cn: 一名护士整夜照料他。

examples.en: The discussion tended toward the question of cost.
examples.cn: 讨论逐渐转向成本问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “探的”——探着身子往一个方向去，也探身照看病人 → tend 倾向、照料

root: 两个来源合流：“倾向”义出自拉丁 tendere“伸展”（经古法语 tendre）；“照料”义是 attend 的缩略，出自拉丁 attendere“留心”（ad- + tendere）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of tend, split between two histories: a stretching toward (inclination, direction, convergence) and an attention turned toward (care, herding, service). Both are forms of leaning out of oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: tend 的九个义项分属两段历史：朝某物伸展（倾向、方向、收敛）与把注意转向某物（照料、放牧、服侍）。两者都是自我向外倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line stretched toward a point, and a herder's gaze stretched toward a flock.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条朝某点伸展的线，与牧人朝羊群伸去的目光。

branches.en: HABIT: behaviour leans in a predictable direction.
branches.cn: 习惯：行为朝可预测的方向倾斜。

branches.en: DIRECTION AND LIMIT: paths and sequences stretch toward a point.
branches.cn: 方向与极限：路径与序列朝某点伸展。

branches.en: CARE: attention is turned toward a person, a fire, or a machine that needs upkeep.
branches.cn: 照料：注意力转向需要维护的人、炉火或机器。

branches.en: SERVICE: bars, flocks, and lords are all kept by a presence that stays.
branches.cn: 服侍：酒吧、羊群与领主，都靠一种留守的在场维持。

branches.en: THE UNFINISHED MIND: a group can tend toward a view without having reached it.
branches.cn: 未完成的心智：群体可以趋向某观点而尚未抵达。

intro.en: Tend's English family splits along its two origins: tendency belongs to the 'stretch' verb, while attend and its derivatives belong to the 'heed' verb. The ten- root also gives tense, tension, tendon, intend, and extend.
intro.cn: tend 的英语词族沿两个来源分裂：tendency 属“伸展”动词，attend 及其派生属“留心”动词。ten- 词根还给出 tense、tension、tendon、intend、extend。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere 'stretch' has the participle tensus, source of tense and tension. Latin attendere 'stretch toward' is ad- plus tendere, and its French shortening gave the care sense of tend. The same *ten- root underlies tendon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tendere“伸展”的分词 tensus 是 tense 与 tension 的来源。拉丁 attendere“朝…伸展”是 ad- 加 tendere，其法语缩略给出 tend 的照料义。同一 *ten- 词根支撑 tendon。

有倾向性的；带偏见的（形容词）

to stretch the mind toward; to plan

definition_zh: 倾向；趋势；癖性
definition_en: a leaning or inclination toward a particular kind of behaviour, direction or outcome
core_image: 一枚小球放在微微倾斜的桌面上，手一松，它总是往同一个方向滚
scene: 议事厅里，同一批人每次表决都往同一个方向靠，连反对者也渐渐跟着举手。There was a clear tendency for the committee to side with the older members.
sceneCN: 这里本词指群体在反复选择中表现出的固定偏向（第 1 个义项：一般倾向）；句意为委员会明显倾向于站在年长成员一边。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到动词，语义为「趋向；倾向」
由同一词根加表「带有倾向」的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「有偏向的」
由上一形容词加副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「带有偏向地」
由上一形容词加名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「偏向性」

senses.title: A general leaning
senses.definition: a general leaning of people or things toward one kind of behaviour or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物总体上偏向某一类行为或结果的态势
senses.example: There is a general tendency for prices to rise before holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 节前价格上涨存在一种普遍倾向。
senses.why: The word began as a stretched direction, and the first sense is that leaning seen in a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 本词最初指被拉伸的方向，第一个义项就是整个群体表现出的这种偏向。

senses.title: A personal habit of mind
senses.definition: a person's habitual inclination to act or feel in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在行为或感受上习惯性的偏向
senses.example: She has a tendency to interrupt when she is nervous.
senses.exampleCN: 她紧张时有打断别人的癖性。
senses.why: A single person also leans one way again and again, and the word names that private tilt.
senses.whyCN: 单个人也会一次次往同一侧倾，本词就指这种私人的偏向。

senses.title: A statistical movement
senses.definition: the direction in which a set of figures moves over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一组数据在一段时间内变动的方向
senses.example: The figures show an upward tendency in household savings.
senses.exampleCN: 数据显示家庭储蓄呈上升趋势。
senses.why: Numbers plotted over time lean visibly, and that lean is what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 按时间画出的数据会显出倾斜，本词描述的正是这种倾斜。

senses.title: A current of opinion
senses.definition: a broad drift of opinion or policy in a society at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期社会舆论或政策上广泛出现的走向
senses.example: A reformist tendency gained ground among younger voters.
senses.exampleCN: 改革倾向在年轻选民中占了上风。
senses.why: When many minds lean together, the lean becomes a public current rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的心思同时倾斜，这种倾斜就成了公共潮流而非私人情绪。

senses.title: A physical drift
senses.definition: the direction in which a body or substance naturally moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 物体或物质自然移动或变化的方向
senses.example: Hot air has a tendency to rise above cooler air.
senses.exampleCN: 热空气有升到冷空气之上的趋向。
senses.why: The oldest image is physical: something stretched or pulled toward a point.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是物理性的：某物被拉向某一点。

senses.title: A medical susceptibility
senses.definition: a bodily weakness that makes a person likely to develop a particular illness
senses.definitionCN: 身体上的弱点使人容易患上某种疾病
senses.example: The condition runs in families with a tendency to low bone density.
senses.exampleCN: 该病多见于有骨密度偏低易感性的家族。
senses.why: A body leaning toward illness is described with the same word as any other lean.
senses.whyCN: 身体向疾病倾斜，用的仍是与其它倾斜相同的词。

senses.title: A stylistic leaning in art
senses.definition: a recurring preference for certain forms or moods in an artist's work
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家作品中反复出现的对某些形式或情绪的偏好
senses.example: His later novels show a tendency toward long, quiet scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 他后期的小说显出偏爱篇幅长而安静的场景。
senses.why: Style is a repeated lean of the hand, and critics borrowed the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 风格是手反复倾斜的结果，评论者便借用这个词来指它。

senses.title: A market drift
senses.definition: the direction in which prices or demand appear to be heading
senses.definitionCN: 价格或需求看起来正在走向的方向
senses.example: Traders watched the tendency of the index for the week.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员盯着这一周指数的走势。
senses.why: Markets are read as leaning one way, so forecasters speak of a tendency rather than a certainty.
senses.whyCN: 市场被看作正在往一侧倾，故预测者说倾向而不说定论。

intro.en: Tendency comes from the Latin verb for stretching or aiming, through a medieval Latin noun for a leaning; it is not related to the word for a trend, which comes from an Old English verb for turning.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，经中世纪拉丁语表「倾斜」的名词进入英语；它与表「走势」的那个词并不同源，后者出自古英语中表「转动」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to stretch out, hold out or aim, and the image is a body or a line extended toward a point.
items.cn: 这一拉丁动词意为「伸出、朝向、瞄准」，意象是身体或线条朝某一点展开。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed a noun from the participle of that verb, naming a leaning or an inclination.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用该动词的分词造出名词，指倾斜或倾向。

items.en: English took the noun in the seventeenth century for a leaning of mind, body or fortune.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入该名词，指心思、身体或运势上的偏向。

items.en: The word for a trend is not a relative: it comes from an Old English verb meaning to turn or revolve, and only later came to mean a direction.
items.cn: 表「走势」的那个词并非同族：它出自古英语中表「转动、旋转」的动词，后来才引申为方向。

items.en: Source uncertain: the older shape of the Latin verb is generally reconstructed, and the first English citation of the noun is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一拉丁动词的更早形态一般为重构，该名词在英语中的最早书证年代亦无确说。

note.en: Group one collects forms that look or sound close to this noun; group two collects words for leanings of mind or body.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的形式；第二组是表示心思或身体偏向的词。

entries.definition: A true relative: the verb means to be inclined or to take care of, and the noun adds a suffix of state.
entries.definitionCN: 确为同源：动词表示趋向或照管，名词则加上表状态的后缀。

entries.definition: It means pushing a one-sided view, built on the same leaning root with an adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 意为推行片面观点，由同一表「倾斜」的词根加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Often treated as a synonym but a different word: it comes from an Old English verb for turning, not from the Latin verb for stretching, so the two are not cognate.
entries.definitionCN: 常被当作同义词，其实是另一个词：它出自古英语表「转动」的动词，而非拉丁语表「伸展」的动词，二者并无同源关系。

entries.definition: It sounds almost the same but comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold, and it names the right to occupy property rather than a leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 读音几乎相同，却出自拉丁语表「握持」的动词，指占用房产的权利，与偏向无关。

entries.definition: A leaning of mind or body, closer to a settled preference than to a measured direction in figures.
entries.definitionCN: 心思或身体上的倾斜，更接近固定的偏好，而非数据中被测量的方向。

entries.definition: A strong natural tendency to behave in a particular way, usually toward something undesirable.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈而天生的行为偏向，通常指向不受欢迎的事。

entries.definition: A person's habitual temperament, the whole cast of mind rather than one lean.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人习惯的性情，是整个心性而非单一偏向。

entries.definition: A slow general movement or change of opinion, stressing gradual motion rather than a built-in lean.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的整体移动或舆论变化，强调渐进，而非内在的倾斜。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to stretch: a line pulled toward a point, and that is the image of the whole family.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为伸展：一条被拉向某点的线，这就是整个词族的意象。

normal.en: The family runs tendency, tend, tendentious, tendentiously, tendentiousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括倾向、趋向、有偏向的、带有偏向地与偏向性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a tendency to overreact, a downward tendency, a growing tendency.
normal.cn: 固定说法：过度反应的倾向、下降趋势、日益增长的趋势。

normal.en: Keep it apart from the word for a trend: that one came from an old verb for turning, not from stretching.
normal.cn: 要与表「走势」的那个词分开：后者出自表「转动」的古动词，并非出自「伸展」。

normal.en: Statistics speak of a tendency when a line on a chart slants; medicine speaks of one when a body is likely to fall ill.
normal.cn: 统计学说倾向，是指图表上的线出现斜度；医学说倾向，是指身体容易生病。

abstract.en: Picture a metal ball rolling toward the low edge of a tilted table, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗金属球一次次滚向倾斜桌面的低边。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one side of a square without anyone giving an order.
abstract.cn: 想象人群没有接到任何指令，却慢慢移向广场的一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that always reaches for the same pen, even when another lies closer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手总去拿同一支笔，哪怕另一支离得更近。

examples.en: Prices show a tendency to fall after the harvest.
examples.cn: 收成之后价格显出下跌的倾向。

examples.en: He has a tendency to talk over people in meetings.
examples.cn: 他在会上有抢别人话头的癖性。

examples.en: The survey found a tendency toward smaller households.
examples.cn: 调查发现家庭规模有变小的趋势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「伸展」记成一条被拉向某处的线：线往哪边斜，就是往哪边倾向。

root: 来自拉丁语中表「伸展、朝向」的动词，中世纪拉丁语由其分词构成表「倾斜」的名词，英语借入后指各种偏向；与表「走势」的词不同源，后者出自古英语表「转动」的动词；更深来源一般为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one model: a line or a body stretched toward one point, so that it leans the same way each time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个模型展开：一条线或一具身体被拉向某一点，于是每次都往同一侧倾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a tilted table, always rolling to the same low corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：倾斜桌面上的球，总滚向同一个低角。

branches.en: LEANING LINE: the general lean of people and the physical drift of matter share one image of a stretched line.
branches.cn: 倾斜的线：人群的整体偏向与物质的物理趋向共享「被拉长的线」这一意象。

branches.en: PRIVATE LEAN: one person's repeated tilt becomes a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 私人偏向：一个人反复的倾斜成为心理习性。

branches.en: MEASURED SLANT: charts and markets are read as leaning, so the word names a direction in figures.
branches.cn: 可测的斜度：图表与市场都被读作倾斜，本词于是指数据中的方向。

branches.en: PUBLIC CURRENT: many minds leaning together become a drift of opinion.
branches.cn: 公共潮流：许多心思同时倾斜，便成舆论走向。

branches.en: BODY AND ART: a body likely to fall ill and a hand that prefers certain forms both lean in the same old sense.
branches.cn: 身体与艺术：易患病的身体与偏爱某些形式的手，都在同一古老意义上倾斜。

intro.en: The noun is built from a Latin verb and a suffix of state, and English keeps a small family around it, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁语动词加表状态的后缀构成，英语周围还保留少量同族词，因此可以按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb supplies the stretching, the Latin participle supplies the leaning, and English supplies only the closing noun suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词提供「伸展」，拉丁语分词提供「倾斜」，英语只提供收尾的名词后缀。

items.example: The root shows in extend, intend and tension, all about stretching.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根见于延伸、打算、张力等词，都与伸展有关。

items.example: A bowstring is stretched, and so is a plan toward its aim.
items.exampleCN: 弓弦被拉紧，计划也朝目标伸展。

items.example: The participle describes what is already leaning.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词描述已经在倾斜的东西。

items.structure: tendens plus a medieval Latin noun suffix
items.example: The medieval noun turned the act of leaning into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪名词把倾斜这一动作变成一种事物。

items.meaning: a leaning toward a kind of act or outcome
items.example: A tendency can be measured over many cases.
items.exampleCN: 倾向可以在许多个案上被测量出来。

items.example: The report was tendentious from its first line.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告从第一行起就带有偏向。

items.meaning: the quality of pushing a lean
items.example: Readers objected to the tendentiousness of the piece.
items.exampleCN: 读者反对这篇文章的偏向性。

items.structure: Latin prefix plus the root tend-
items.example: They extended the deadline by a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们把截止期限延长了一周。

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch, to extend, to aim

definition_zh: 温柔的；嫩的；疼痛的；正式提出；投标；照管者
definition_en: gentle and careful; easily painful; or to offer something formally; also a formal offer or a caregiver
core_image: 碰一下就皱眉的嫩芽，也是递出标书时轻放的手
scene: 照看幼苗的人连浇水都放轻了手。The young plants need tender care in the first weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 tender 是形容词「精心呵护的、温柔的」（第 1 个义项：温柔体贴的）；句意：幼苗头几周需要温柔细致的照料。

derivatives.zh: 温柔地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
温柔；触痛（形容词加 -ness 构成）
使肉变嫩（形容词加 -ize 动词后缀）

senses.title: Gentle, loving and careful
senses.definition: showing gentleness, kindness and care
senses.definitionCN: 表现出温柔、善意与呵护
senses.example: She gave the rescued kitten tender care.
senses.exampleCN: 她悉心照料获救的小猫。
senses.why: The image is the young shoot: what is soft needs and receives a soft touch.
senses.whyCN: 意象是嫩芽：柔弱之物需要也召来轻柔的触碰。

senses.title: Soft and easy to cut or chew
senses.definition: soft and easy to bite, used of meat or plants
senses.definitionCN: 柔软易咬的，用于肉或植物
senses.example: Slow cooking makes the beef tender.
senses.exampleCN: 慢炖使牛肉软嫩。
senses.why: Physical softness is the literal shoot image: tender flesh yields to the touch.
senses.whyCN: 物理的柔嫩是「嫩芽」意象的直取：嫩肉一按即让。

senses.title: Painful when touched
senses.definition: sensitive or painful to touch, used of skin or muscles
senses.definitionCN: 触碰即痛，用于皮肤或肌肉
senses.example: The bruise is still tender.
senses.exampleCN: 淤伤一按还疼。
senses.why: The shoot also flinches: what is soft hurts when pressed.
senses.whyCN: 嫩芽也会躲闪：柔弱之处一经按压便喊疼。

senses.title: To offer something formally
senses.definition: to present something officially, such as a resignation or a bid
senses.definitionCN: 正式呈递某物，如辞呈或标书
senses.example: He tendered his resignation this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他今早正式递交辞呈。
senses.why: A formal offer is handled with both hands, gently placed: the same soft touch, now ceremonial.
senses.whyCN: 正式呈递之物以双手轻放：同一种轻柔触碰，只是此番带上仪式感。

senses.title: A formal offer or bid
senses.definition: a written offer to do work or supply goods at a fixed price
senses.definitionCN: 按定价承接工程或供货的书面报价
senses.example: Five companies submitted tenders for the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 五家公司提交了大桥工程投标。
senses.why: The offer itself is named by the gesture: the placed document is a tender.
senses.whyCN: 报价以那个动作命名：被轻轻放上桌的文件，就叫 tender。

senses.title: A person or boat that attends another
senses.titleCN: 照管者；随侍人员；补给船
senses.definition: a person or small boat that serves or attends to a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 照看他人或为主船服务的小船或人员
senses.example: The bar tender kept everyone's glasses full.
senses.exampleCN: 酒吧侍者让大家的杯子一直满着。
senses.why: The one who tends is named after the care itself: attendance is tenderness in work clothes.
senses.whyCN: 照管者以「照料」为名：随侍就是穿上工装的温柔。

intro.en: English has two tenders. The soft one comes from Latin tener, delicate, through Old French tendre. The offer one comes from tendere, to stretch toward, the same root as tend.
intro.cn: 英语有两个 tender。「柔嫩」的 tender 出自拉丁语 tener「柔嫩」，经古法语 tendre 传入；「提出、投标」的 tender 出自 tendere「朝…伸去」，与 tend 同根。

items.en: Tener meant delicate, soft, young; its deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: tener 意为柔嫩、幼小；其更深词根不确定。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch toward, and its participle tensus gives tense.
items.cn: tendere 意为朝某方向拉伸，分词 tensus 生成 tense。

items.en: Old French tendre carried both Latin words, soft and stretching, into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tendre 把拉丁两词——柔嫩与拉伸——一并带入英语。

items.en: English borrowed tendre twice: the soft adjective and the offer verb.
items.cn: 英语两度借入 tendre：柔嫩的形容词与呈递的动词。

items.en: Commerce fixed the bid sense, medicine kept the pain sense, and cooking kept the meat sense.
items.cn: 商业固定投标义，医学保留触痛义，烹饪保留嫩肉义。

note.en: The two tenders are distinguished from each other and set beside softness words.
note.cn: 区分两个 tender，并将其与表示柔软的词并列。

entries.definition: to incline or care for; shares the stretch root with the offer tender
entries.definitionCN: 倾向；照料；与「提出」义的 tender 同根

entries.definition: in a gentle way
entries.definitionCN: 温柔地

entries.definition: the cord that stretches muscle to bone
entries.definitionCN: 肌腱；连接肌肉与骨骼的拉紧之索

entries.definition: mild and kind in manner
entries.definitionCN: 温和的；和善的

entries.definition: not hard or firm
entries.definitionCN: 软的；不坚硬的

entries.definition: a formal offer of a price
entries.definitionCN: 出价；投标（对照词）

normalIntro.en: Real links: tener soft, tendere stretch, the bid on the table, and tender age.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tener「柔嫩」、tendere「拉伸」、桌上的标书、tender age。

normal.en: Tener means delicate: a tender leaf bends before it breaks.
normal.cn: tener 意为柔嫩：嫩叶先弯后折。

normal.en: Tendere means stretch toward: you tender a document by stretching out your hand.
normal.cn: tendere 意为朝…伸去：tender 文件就是把手伸出去。

normal.en: Tender meat has yielded to slow fire.
normal.cn: 嫩肉是向文火投降的肉。

normal.en: Tender age: the soft years that flinch at every touch.
normal.cn: tender age：一碰就缩的柔弱年岁。

normal.en: A bid called a tender is placed, not thrown.
normal.cn: 被称为 tender 的标书是「轻放」而非「抛出」的。

abstract.en: Softness is strength that has agreed to be careful.
abstract.cn: 柔是同意小心行事的力。

abstract.en: The hand that gives is the same hand that soothes.
abstract.cn: 给予的手与安抚的手是同一只手。

abstract.en: What flinches teaches the world to touch slowly.
abstract.cn: 会缩的东西教会世界放慢触碰。

examples.en: The nurse handled the wound with tender hands.
examples.cn: 护士用温柔的手处理伤口。

examples.en: The company tendered for the new tunnel project.
examples.cn: 该公司投标了新隧道工程。

examples.en: Steamed fish should be tender, not tough.
examples.cn: 蒸鱼应当软嫩，不能老韧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「疼得」——伤口疼得一碰就缩，得轻点碰 → tender 触痛的、温柔的

root: 两个来源：「柔嫩」义出自拉丁语 tener「嫩的」（经古法语 tendre）；「提出、投标、照管」义出自拉丁语 tendere「朝…伸去」（ad- + tendere 的 attend/tend 一族）。

sensesIntro.en: Two histories meet in one spelling: the shoot that bends, and the hand stretched out with an offer.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种历史共用一个拼写：会弯的嫩芽，与递出报价时伸出的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young shoot, and an outstretched hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株嫩芽，与一只伸出的手。

branches.en: Softness of manner and of meat share one leaf.
branches.cn: 态度之柔与肉质之嫩共用一片嫩叶。

branches.en: The shoot flinches when pressed.
branches.cn: 嫩芽被按便闪躲。

branches.en: The stretched hand presents the bid.
branches.cn: 伸出的手呈递标书。

branches.en: The tender of a ship attends the large one.
branches.cn: 补给船随侍大船。

branches.en: Care is softness given a job.
branches.cn: 照料是被派了任务的柔软。

intro.en: Tender stands between two Latin roots: tener, soft, and tendere, stretch.
intro.cn: tender 处于两个拉丁词根之间：tener「柔嫩」与 tendere「拉伸」。

latinIntro.en: Latin tener means delicate; Latin tendere means to stretch toward; both reached English through Old French tendre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tener 意为柔嫩；tendere 意为朝…伸去；两者经古法语 tendre 进入英语。

definition_zh: 紧张的；绷紧的；（动词的）时态；使紧张
definition_en: tightly stretched or nervous; also the form of a verb showing time
core_image: 一根被拉到极限的琴弦
scene: 考试铃响前，教室里安静得能听见笔尖。Everyone went tense as the results were announced.
sceneCN: 这里 tense 是形容词「紧张的」（第 1 个义项：精神紧绷）；句意：成绩宣布时所有人都紧张起来。

derivatives.zh: 张力；紧张（分词 tensus 加 -ion 构成）
紧张地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
肌腱（同根名词，被拉紧的索）

senses.title: Nervous and unable to relax
senses.definition: feeling worried and unable to relax
senses.definitionCN: 焦虑不安、无法放松的
senses.example: She felt tense before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她很紧张。
senses.why: The string image: a mind pulled tight like a cord ready to snap.
senses.whyCN: 琴弦意象：心被拉得像一根随时会断的弦。

senses.title: Tightly stretched
senses.definition: stretched tight, used of muscles, ropes or wires
senses.definitionCN: 被拉紧的，用于肌肉、绳索或钢丝
senses.example: Climb with tense arms and steady legs.
senses.exampleCN: 攀岩时手臂绷紧、双腿站稳。
senses.why: This is the literal root sense: the cord pulled to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根的字面义：绳索被拉到极限。

senses.title: A verb form showing time
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows when an action happens
senses.definitionCN: 表明动作发生时间的动词形式
senses.example: English uses the past tense for finished actions.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用过去时表示已完成动作。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the stretched string for time stretched along a line.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了绷紧的弦，来比喻沿时间线拉开的动作。

senses.title: To make a muscle or person tight
senses.definition: to tighten a muscle or make someone anxious
senses.definitionCN: 使肌肉收紧或使人心绪紧张
senses.example: He tensed his shoulders before lifting.
senses.exampleCN: 举重前他绷紧了双肩。
senses.why: The adjective turns into an action: pulling the string on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为动作：主动去拉那根弦。

intro.en: Tense, tight, comes from Latin tendere, to stretch, through its participle tensus. The grammar tense is a separate borrowing of Latin tempus, time.
intro.cn: 「紧绷」的 tense 源自拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」的分词 tensus；语法「时态」的 tense 则另借拉丁语 tempus「时间」。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch; tensus meant stretched tight.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸；tensus 意为绷紧的。

items.en: Tendere is usually traced to a reconstructed PIE root for stretching.
items.cn: tendere 一般被追溯到重构的印欧「拉伸」词根。

items.en: Old French tens passed the tight sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tens 把「绷紧」义传入英语。

items.en: The grammar term entered separately from Old French temps, Latin tempus.
items.cn: 语法术语经古法语 temps（拉丁 tempus）另行进入。

items.en: Spelling merged both words as tense; context tells the time-word from the tight-word.
items.cn: 两词拼合为 tense；语境区分「时间」与「紧绷」。

note.en: Tense is compared with its stretch family and with nerves words.
note.cn: 把 tense 与「拉伸」词族及表示神经紧绷的词对比。

entries.definition: the state of being stretched or strained
entries.definitionCN: 张力；紧张

entries.definition: the cord joining muscle and bone
entries.definitionCN: 肌腱

entries.definition: a stretched cloth shelter
entries.definitionCN: 帐篷；同一拉伸词根的另一产物

entries.definition: worried and frightened about something
entries.definitionCN: 紧张的；不安的

entries.definition: pulled tight, no slack
entries.definitionCN: 拉紧的；不松垮的

entries.definition: pressure or tension on body or mind
entries.definitionCN: 压力；劳损

normalIntro.en: Real links: tensus stretched, the tense-tension-tendon family, and the time word hidden in grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tensus「绷紧」、tense/tension/tendon 词族、藏在语法里的时间词。

normal.en: Tensus means stretched: a tense rope hums when plucked.
normal.cn: tensus 意为绷紧：紧绷的绳一拨就嗡嗡响。

normal.en: Tense up before the dive: pull every string in the body.
normal.cn: 跳水前 tense up：把全身的弦都拉紧。

normal.en: Grammar tense is tempus, time wearing a verb's coat.
normal.cn: 语法 tense 就是 tempus：时间穿着动词的外衣。

normal.en: Tension in the room: everyone is a drawn bow.
normal.cn: 屋里的 tension：人人都像拉满的弓。

normal.en: A tendon is a living rope, always a little tense.
normal.cn: 肌腱是活的绳，永远微微绷着。

abstract.en: A nerve and a wire behave the same when pulled.
abstract.cn: 神经与钢丝被拉紧时表现相同。

abstract.en: Time itself is a string grammar likes to stretch.
abstract.cn: 时间本身就是一根语法爱拉紧的弦。

abstract.en: Relaxation is simply letting the string slack.
abstract.cn: 放松不过是让弦松下来。

examples.en: The room went tense when the verdict was read.
examples.cn: 宣判时屋里气氛骤然紧张。

examples.en: Past tense verbs often end in ed.
examples.cn: 过去式动词常以 ed 结尾。

examples.en: Relax your tense shoulders and breathe.
examples.cn: 放松紧绷的肩膀，深呼吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摊死」——紧张得像摊开又拉死的弦，一动就断 → tense 紧张的、时态

root: 「紧绷」义：拉丁 tendere「拉伸」分词 tensus → 古法语 tens → 英语 tense；「时态」义另借拉丁 tempus「时间」（经古法语 temps），两词拼写合流。

sensesIntro.en: One spelling, two strings: the pulled cord and the stretched line of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个拼写，两根弦：被拉紧的绳与被拉开的时间线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string pulled to its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉到极限的弦。

branches.en: The literal cord, humming.
branches.cn: 字面之弦，嗡嗡作响。

branches.en: The body and the room both tighten.
branches.cn: 身体与房间都会收紧。

branches.en: Grammar keeps time on a line.
branches.cn: 语法把时间排在一条线上。

branches.en: A drawn bow is a waiting sentence.
branches.cn: 拉满的弓是一句等待中的判词。

branches.en: Release is the other half of tense.
branches.cn: 「松开」是 tense 的另一半。

intro.en: Tense shares the tendere stretch family with tension, tendon and tent.
intro.cn: tense 与 tension、tendon、tent 同属 tendere「拉伸」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, to stretch, has the participle tensus, source of the tight sense; the grammar tense is from tempus, time.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」分词 tensus 是「紧绷」义之源；语法义出自 tempus「时间」。

definition_zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的；迟疑不决的
definition_en: not yet final and open to change, or done cautiously as a first test
core_image: 谈判桌上摆着一份还没定稿的备忘录，签字旁边留着一行小字：待双方董事会批准
scene: 谈判结束时，双方在一份仍可修改的备忘录上签了名，各自都留了一步退路。They reached a tentative agreement that still needed approval from both boards.
sceneCN: 这里指尚未最终确定、仍可更改（第 1 个义项：暂定的）；句意为双方达成了一份仍待两家董事会批准的初步协议。图中可辨识物件：备忘录、签名栏、一行待批准的小字、会议桌。

pos.zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「试探性地；暂定地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「试探性；迟疑」
由同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「尝试」，属同源而非直接派生
由同一拉丁动词的另一形态经法语构成，义为「引诱；试探」，属同源而非直接派生

senses.title: Not final
senses.definition: agreed or set for now but still open to change
senses.definitionCN: 暂时确定、但仍可更改的
senses.example: The schedule is tentative and will be confirmed on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 日程是暂定的，周五才会确认。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to try, and what is tried is not yet settled.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「尝试」，试过的东西自然还没有定下来。

senses.title: An initial agreement
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted in outline, pending formal approval
senses.definitionCN: 在要点上接受、等待正式批准的安排
senses.example: The two sides signed a tentative agreement and left the details to their lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签了一份初步协议，细节留给各自的律师。
senses.why: An agreement is tentative while the signatures still wait for approval upstairs.
senses.whyCN: 协议在签名还等着上级批准时，就是初步的。

senses.title: A testing first step
senses.definition: a cautious action taken to see how others react
senses.definitionCN: 为看看对方反应而谨慎采取的行动
senses.example: She took a tentative step into the new market before committing a full budget.
senses.exampleCN: 她先在新市场试探性地迈出一步，之后才投入全部预算。
senses.why: A step that tests the ground keeps the meaning of trying in the body.
senses.whyCN: 试探地面的一步，把「尝试」的含义落到了步子上。

senses.title: A cautious smile
senses.definition: a slight smile that asks whether it is welcome
senses.definitionCN: 轻微地笑一下，试探对方是否接受
senses.example: The new student gave a tentative smile and waited for an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的学生试探性地笑了笑，等着对方回应。
senses.why: Here the uncertainty is social rather than factual, but the same caution shows.
senses.whyCN: 这里的不确定是社会性的而非事实性的，但同样的谨慎仍然可见。

senses.title: A provisional conclusion
senses.definition: a conclusion offered while evidence is still incomplete
senses.definitionCN: 在证据仍不完整时给出的结论
senses.example: Our tentative conclusion is that the effect is small, though more trials are needed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的初步结论是效应不大，但仍需更多试验。
senses.why: A conclusion offered while data are still arriving is held provisionally by design.
senses.whyCN: 在数据仍陆续到来时给出的结论，按设计就是暂且持有的。

senses.title: A date that may move
senses.definition: a fixed date that everyone knows may be changed
senses.definitionCN: 大家都明白可能会改的已定日期
senses.example: We have a tentative date in June, subject to the permit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们暂定六月，还要看许可证。
senses.why: Setting a date provisionally is a way of planning without promising.
senses.whyCN: 把日期暂定下来，是一种「做计划但不作承诺」的办法。

senses.title: A hesitant tone
senses.definition: speaking in a way that shows one is unsure of the welcome
senses.definitionCN: 说话时显出不确定对方是否欢迎的样子
senses.example: He answered in a tentative voice, as if expecting to be corrected.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟疑地回答，好像随时准备被纠正。
senses.why: Caution moves from the plan to the voice, and the word now describes how someone speaks.
senses.whyCN: 谨慎从计划移到声音上，词于是描述一个人怎么说话。

senses.title: Exploratory in method
senses.definition: trying a small move in an unfamiliar situation before going further
senses.definitionCN: 在陌生情境里先小幅行动、再决定是否继续
senses.example: The first meetings were tentative, designed to test whether the teams could work together.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的几次会面是试探性的，用来检验两队是否能合作。
senses.why: A method is tentative when its first purpose is to find out whether it works at all.
senses.whyCN: 当一种方法的首要目的是弄清它究竟行不行，它就是试探性的。

intro.en: Tentative comes from Latin tentativus, trying or testing, from tentare, to try, a frequentative form of tendere, to stretch. English took it in the sixteenth century for statements and steps held only provisionally, and the idea of a trial has stayed at its centre.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 tentativus「尝试的、试探的」，出自动词 tentare「试」，而 tentare 是 tendere「伸展」的反复形式。十六世纪进入英语，用来指只是暂时拿出的说法与步骤，「试一试」的意思始终在核心。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or aim, and its repeated form described trying something again and again.
items.cn: 这个词意为「伸展、指向」，其反复形式表示一次又一次地试。

items.en: Tentare meant to try, to test, and also to attack or probe.
items.cn: 这个词意为「试、试探」，也有「进攻、探察」之意。

items.en: The adjective described what was done by way of trial rather than as a settled act.
items.cn: 该形容词形容出于尝试而非定论所做的。

items.en: French used the adjective for experiments and provisional arrangements.
items.cn: 法语用它指实验与暂定的安排。

items.en: English applied it to opinions, plans and the first movements of a cautious person.
items.cn: 英语把它用于意见、计划以及谨慎者的最初动作。

items.en: Negotiation gave the word its common phrase, tentative agreement; the phrase's first recorded year is uncertain.
items.cn: 谈判给出它最常见的搭配「初步协议」；该搭配首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the trying root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of provisional things. The note also separates tentative from tenable, which looks similar but comes from a different verb.
note.cn: 第一组共享「尝试」词根或形近；第二组指其他「暂时性」的说法。这里也把「暂定的」与形近但异源的「站得住脚的」分开。

entries.definition: In a cautious or provisional way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以试探或暂定的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being provisional or hesitant.
entries.definitionCN: 指暂定或迟疑的性质。

entries.definition: To try to do something; the same Latin verb reached English through French.
entries.definitionCN: 指尝试做某事；同一拉丁动词经法语进入英语。

entries.definition: To lure or test someone; a different form of the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指引诱或试探某人；同一拉丁动词的另一形式。

entries.definition: Able to be defended; it comes from the verb meaning to hold, not to try.
entries.definitionCN: 指站得住脚、可辩护的；出自表示「握住」的动词，与「尝试」无关。

entries.definition: A principle held as true; from the same holding verb as tenable.
entries.definitionCN: 指被奉为真的原则；与「站得住脚」同出「握住」动词。

entries.definition: Arranged for present needs and expected to be replaced.
entries.definitionCN: 指为当前需要而设、预期会被替换的。

entries.definition: Coming before the main event as preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在正式活动之前、作为准备的。

entries.definition: Serving only for the time between two settled states.
entries.definitionCN: 指只在两个稳定状态之间暂时顶替的。

entries.definition: Done in order to find out rather than to settle.
entries.definitionCN: 指为了了解情况而非下定论所做的。

entries.definition: Slow to act because of uncertainty; it describes the person rather than the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指因不确定而行动迟缓，描述的是人而不是安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the unsigned contract, the first small step, the careful smile and the June date pencilled in.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用未定稿的备忘录、试探的一小步、谨慎的微笑与用铅笔写下的六月。

normal.en: A tentative deal is written in pencil, not in ink.
normal.cn: 初步协议用铅笔写，不用墨水。

normal.en: A tentative step is a foot testing the ice before the body follows.
normal.cn: 试探性的一步，是脚先试试冰面，身体再跟上。

normal.en: A tentative smile asks a question without words.
normal.cn: 试探性的微笑，是在不用言语地问一句。

normal.en: If the date is tentative, the invitation says so and nobody is blamed.
normal.cn: 日期若为暂定，请柬上会写明，事后也没人该被责怪。

normal.en: Tentative and tenable look alike, but one means tried and the other means holdable.
normal.cn: 「暂定的」与「站得住脚的」形近，一个意为「试过」，一个意为「握得住」。

abstract.en: Provisional things are honest about their own fragility, which is why they are trusted for a while.
abstract.cn: 暂定之物坦白自己的脆弱，所以反而能被信任一阵。

abstract.en: Every firm decision began as a tentative one that someone dared to repeat.
abstract.cn: 每个确定的决定，起初都是一个有人敢重复的暂定决定。

abstract.en: To try is to leave a door open; to settle is to close it, and both have their season.
abstract.cn: 尝试是留一扇门，确定是把门关上，两者各有其时。

examples.en: The committee adopted a tentative plan and asked for cost estimates.
examples.cn: 委员会采纳了一项暂定计划，并要求提供成本估算。

examples.en: He gave a tentative nod, then asked to see the contract again.
examples.cn: 他试探性地点了点头，随后要求再看一遍合同。

examples.en: The tentative date is 12 June, subject to the venue.
examples.cn: 暂定日期是六月十二日，还要看场地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦特提夫」：先「试」一下再说话，语气留半分，结论也留半分

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「伸展、指向」的动词，其反复形式义为「试、试探」，再加形容词尾，经法语进入英语。表示「尝试」「引诱」的英语词与之同源，但不是由它直接派生。十六世纪进入英语；「初步协议」这一搭配首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one caution: a provisional arrangement, an initial deal, a testing step, a cautious smile, a provisional conclusion, a movable date, a hesitant voice, and an exploratory method.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一种谨慎：暂定安排、初步协议、试探的一步、谨慎的微笑、初步结论、可改的日期、迟疑的语气与试探性的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature goes on a memorandum that still carries a line asking for later approval.
core.cn: 核心意象：名字签在一份备忘录上，旁边还留着一行「待批准」。

branches.en: THE OPEN ARRANGEMENT: a plan or date that everyone knows may move.
branches.cn: 敞开的安排：人人都知道可能会变的计划或日期。

branches.en: THE FIRST VERSION: an initial deal or conclusion, subject to approval.
branches.cn: 最初版本：初步协议或结论，仍待批准。

branches.en: THE FIRST PROBE: a small action taken to read another person's reaction.
branches.cn: 探路的一步：先做一个动作，看看对方如何反应。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL HESITATION: a careful smile and a careful voice.
branches.cn: 社交上的迟疑：谨慎的微笑与谨慎的语气。

branches.en: EXPLORATORY BY METHOD: start small in an unfamiliar setting, then decide whether to continue.
branches.cn: 方法上的试探：在陌生情境里先做小步，再决定是否继续。

intro.en: Tentative is a Latin trying verb with two endings; its family covers trying, testing and the caution that goes with both.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「试」动词加词尾；词族覆盖尝试、试探以及随之而来的谨慎。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, tentare and tentativus trace the path from stretching to trying to provisional.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「伸展」「试」「尝试的」三词，勾出从拉伸到尝试再到暂定的路径。
